articleTitle: Fundamental Limits of Covert Communications Covered by Randomly Activated Overt Users
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper studies the fundamental limits of the amount of information that can be transmitted in covert communications covered by randomly activated overt users. First, an upper bound is developed with a novel recursive-iterative approximation on the intractable total variation distance (TVD) to measure the detection probability of the warden, which is tighter than the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD). On this basis, the collapse effect of the TVD is revealed, which shows that the TVD is strictly less than 1 if the covert user sets the transmit power to be an integer multiple of that of the overt users. Then, we find that up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N)$</tex> bits of information can be reliably and covertly transmitted over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> channel uses under the above power setting, which breaks the well-known square root law. If the above power setting is violated, still, the TVD will instantly approach 1 as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\rightarrow \infty$</tex>, and only no more than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(\sqrt{N})$</tex> bits can be covertly transmitted. To prove this, the detection method of the warden is modified to cope with the random activation of the users. The above conclusions also hold even if the transmit powers of the overt users are randomly distributed, which resembles realistic wireless transmissions.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Identifying Critical Nodes in Networks Based on Spectral Clustering to Construct Hypergraphs
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Currently, the basis for critical nodes definition and identification lies in the representation learning of the network and the extraction of local and global features of the nodes. The effectiveness of the algorithm is closely related to network modeling and network structural characteristics. However, with the increasing complexity of real-world systems, utilizing the continuity and integrity of traditional bipartite graph representation faces significant challenges. Different from traditional graph modeling, the hyperedges of a hypergraph can connect multiple nodes simultaneously, thus forming richer structural features and interaction information between nodes for the analysis and judgment of critical nodes. To more accurately identify critical nodes in complex networks, we propose an algorithm that establishes a hypergraph representation for traditional graph data to extract higher-order features of nodes for neural network training, in order to identify critical nodes in complex networks. The effectiveness of this method is proven by comparing it with various critical node identification algorithms under different infection rates.

articleTitle: Achievable Rate Analysis of UAV-Mounted RIS-Assisted Link with UAV 3D Location Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) can enhance the communication performance by contributing a virtual line-of-sight (VLoS) link between the transceivers when the LoS path is blocked. However, conventional terrestrial deployed RISs are limited to half-space reflection with restricted locations. In this paper, we consider the deployment of RIS on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), which is also referred to as UAV-mounted RIS, to explore its advantages in full-space reflection and flexible mobility. We first develop a novel channel model for the proposed UAV-mounted RIS-assisted multiple input multiple output (MIMO) communications in the presence of three-dimensional (3D) location variation of the UAV-mounted RIS. Based on the proposed model, the link achievable rate is derived as a metric to investigate the impact brought by the location variation. Numerical results are provided to verify the accuracy of our derived results.

articleTitle: Towards Task-Scalable Semantic Communications: A Preprocessing Enhanced Image Transmission Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Recently, more and more images are transmitted to the receiver for the machine analysis tasks instead of purely for the human-vision task. However, most current machine-type semantic communication systems are optimized towards a specific task or a given set of tasks, without considering the scalability to new tasks. In this work, we propose a preprocessing enhanced image semantic communication system to address this challenge. Instead of optimizing directly towards a specific task, our system first optimizes a neural codec for preserving the holistic image information under the trade-off between bandwidth and distortion. Then, we reveal that the performance drop on the primary task can be ascribed to a lack of generalization of the task head to images with overall artifacts caused by compression and noisy channels. Accordingly, by finetuning a preprocessing module based on the pretrained neural codec under the trade-off between task accuracy and distortion, most loss on the primary task accuracy can be recovered with a trivial degradation on distortion, in this way, the task-scalable ability can also be preserved well due to the high quality on the holistic image. Experiments verify the effectiveness of our method in driving the primary task and the scalability to new tasks.

articleTitle: FoV Improvement Through Dual-Lens Fiber Coupling for Optical Mobile Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Optical mobile communication (OMC) systems employ lasers to transfer data, and they are famous for the abundant spectrum and high security. With the acquisition, tracking, and pointing (ATP) mechanisms, transmitters of the OMC systems can track and steer laser beams to the receivers, making the transceivers capable of serving mobile users. However, the receivers need precise mechanics to adjust the direction of the incident laser before coupling it into the fiber, and this coupling system usually has too low field-of-view (FoV) for mobile receivers. In this paper, we propose a novel dual-lens structure to couple the free-space laser beam into a multi-mode fiber. The average optical power coupling efficiency of the Gaussian laser spot with random radial pointing errors is derived. The results of theory, simulation and experiment are consistent and show that the FoV of the dual-lens receiver is larger than the single-lens receiver, and the outage probability of OMC can be suppressed by employing the dual-lens coupler.

articleTitle: RFF Recognition Based on Adaptive Signal Transform and Weighted Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) is an effective physical layer identification technique that makes Internet of Things (IoT) systems more secure. It uses the deviation of the parameters of each electronic component in the transmitter from the nominal parameters to perform the authentication task. RFF recognition schemes based on deep learning (DL) are emerging due to their ability to automatically perform feature extraction and classification. To fully exploit the information in RF signals, researchers perform feature extraction from different signal representations and fuse these features for subsequent classification tasks. However, selecting the combination of signal representations is a time-consuming task. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an RFF recognition model based on Adaptive Signal Transform (AST) and Weighted Feature Fusion (WFF). The AST module is able to learn a signal transform form, which can greatly improve recognition accuracy and reduce the pressure of manual selection of signal representations. In addition, we use multiple convolution layers to form the WFF module. This module weighs the RFF features and highlights the feature components that favor classification. Simulation results show the ability of these modules to improve the performance of RFF recognition and the effectiveness of the proposed AST-WFF model.

articleTitle: HRC-Net : A High Robust ConvNeXt for Noisy Image
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Despite the fairly good performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in image classification tasks, existing CNNs do not perform well when handling datasets with Gaussian noise. This results in the instability of model performance under extreme conditions or due to device aging. To address this issue, this paper introduces parameter-free attention and employs a simple wavelet decomposition and reconstruction method for image preprocessing, which minimizes the impact of noise on the model's performance. When the noise ratio is 40%, the accuracy of the improved model is approximately 90.4%, representing an increase of 3.1% compared to the original model's accuracy of 87.3%. This indicates that the proposed model in this paper is less sensitive to the impact of Gaussian noise, demonstrating its high robustness.

articleTitle: Fast Erasure Decoding of Reed-Solomon Codes Based on Decomposition of Vandermonde Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Reed-Solomon (RS) codes are widely applied in storage systems. The main bottleneck of RS codes is that the high decoding complexity defined as the number of multiplications and additions. In this paper, we propose a fast decoding algorithm for RS codes that requires fewer number of multiplications. Our fast decoding algorithm is designed by a decomposition of Vandermonde matrices. We show that our decoding algorithm requires fewer number of multiplications than the existing best known algorithm when the number of parities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> is large. When the codeword length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=16$</tex>, our decoding algorithm reduces the number of multiplications by 7% and 29% when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T=4$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T=7$</tex>, respectively, compared with the best known decoding algorithm.

articleTitle: Training Quantum Self-Attention Model in Near-Term Quantum Computer
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly emerging as a revolutionary computing paradigm with significant development potential. Variational quantum algorithms, especially those employing variational quantum circuits, have demonstrated notable advantages in domains including finance, chemistry, and machine learning. However, the practical deployment of these algorithms on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices faces challenges due to quantum noise, state collapse, and limited qubits numbers. The real-world performance of these algorithms remains largely unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by proposing and implementing a novel method for training quantum self-attention model for text classification directly on quantum computing chips. This initiative marks the first instance of employing such models on actual quantum hardware. Our approach optimizes quantum circuit designs to mitigate the impact of quantum noise and introduces parallel training strategies to enhance efficiency. Our experiments, conducted on the “Wukong” superconducting 72-qubit quantum computer, demonstrate that our models can be effectively trained on real quantum hardware. The results from the actual quantum chips slightly outperformed those from simulators, confirming the practical feasibility of applying quantum self-attention model to natural language processing tasks. These results validate the effectiveness of our approach and provide valuable insights for the future deployment of quantum machine learning models.

articleTitle: Joint Design for Energy Replenishment and Data Collection in AUV-Based Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) rely heavily on data collection from underwater sensors, which is crucial for the functionality of these networks. However, the limited energy of sensors depletes over time as tasks are performed, leading to sensor failures and subsequently reducing the network's lifespan. While most existing research introduces autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) for close-range data collection to mitigate sensor energy consumption, this method cannot prevent the ultimate death of the network. To enhance the functionality of UWSNs, we jointly consider energy replenishment and data collection for UWSNs. Therefore, an AUV-based charging and data collection scheme (CDCS) is proposed. CDCS will allow the AUV to charge sensors closely and plan a charging path for the AUV. In addition, CDCS proposes that during the charging time of sensors, the AUV performs cluster-based data collection from sensors to fully utilize the charging time. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of the scheme.

articleTitle: Target Parameter Estimation for PMCW Radar Equipped with One-Bit Mod-ADC-K
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: We consider target parameter estimation for automotive Phase-Modulated Continuous-Wave (PMCW) radar equipped with one-bit modulo analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) with known folding-counts (Mod-ADC-K). One-bit Mod-ADC-K can save energy and overcome the dynamic range problems of one-bit or low-bit conventional ADCs. And the Iterative Adaptive Approach (IAA) is a robust nonparametric spectral estimation algorithm with high resolution. However, each one-bit Mod-ADC-K introduces an additional folding, which makes the conventional one-bit IAA unusable, so it is necessary to devise new target parameter estimation algorithms. We introduce an extended IAA algorithm, referred to as Mod-IAA for one-bit Mod-ADC-K based target parameter estimation. Finally, we provide numerical examples to demonstrate the advantages of using one-bit Mod-Adc-K for target parameter estimation using PMCW radar.

articleTitle: Channel Characteristic Analysis and Modeling of WBAN at 11GHz in Medical Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To explore the feasibility of high-frequency band indoor wireless body area network (WBAN) communication in hospital environments, the propagation characteristics of indoor WBAN at the 11GHz are measured and studied. Based on measured data, the statistical characteristics of path loss (PL), shadowing effect and root mean square delay spread (RMS-DS) are analyzed. In the case of height difference between the transmitter and receiver, the PL model with the patient's body angle effect is proposed, where the body angle can be either a horizontal rotation angle or a vertical rotation angle. The research results show that the PL caused by the body angle in the horizontal direction has quadratic function relation with body angle, and it has a trigonometric relationship with the body angle in the vertical direction. In addition, the changes in body angle in different directions also have different impacts on RMS-DS. The above research results can provide a theoretical and practical foundation for the future use of high-frequency bands in indoor medical scenarios.

articleTitle: Impacts of Blockages on UAV-Enabled Integrated Sensing and Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impacts of block-ages on the performances of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Specifically, we first derive the distance distribution between UAV and a typical target in both communication and sensing scenarios, in the presence of three-dimensional blockages. Compared to previous models that either ignored blockage effects or considered only in two-dimensional plane, our model provides a more realistic characterization of random blockages in UAV-enabled ISAC systems. Then, we leverage the tools from stochastic geometry to derive the analytical expressions of the communication coverage probability and successful detection probability in our considered system. Finally, we validate our analysis through numerical results and reveal the interactions between communication and sensing performances, under the impacts of blockages.

articleTitle: STDF-DSCS: A Lightweight Scheme for Compressed Video Quality Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Lossy compression reduces the data amount in the video by sacrificing quality, which leads to severe distortion, especially when videos are overly compressed. Con-sequently, many restoration methods have been proposed to repair compressed videos. However, they are limited by their substantial computational demand and complexity. To conserve computational resources and enhance real-time capabilities, we implement a compressed video enhancement method based on Spatio-Temporal Deformable Fusion (STDF) and subsequently design a lightweight scheme for it. By integrating depthwise separable convolution and channel shuffle techniques, we design a lightweight version of STDF called STDF-DSCS. STDF-DSCS reduces computational complexity and improves model inference speed while maintaining enhancement quality. The depthwise separable convolution reduces the model's computational complexity, while channel shuffle compensates for the shortcomings of group convolution, enhancing inter-channel communication and the network's feature learning capability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that STDF-DSCS significantly enhances computational efficiency while maintaining comparable enhancement effects to existing methods, which can be utilized in real-time video processing scenarios.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz to 5G-Advanced: Multifrequency Channel Measurements, Modeling, and Characteristics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Multifrequency cooperative wireless networking will become a critical development trend to fulfill the specific requirements in the future of 5G-Advanced and beyond wireless systems. However, the wide frequency range will introduce new propagation properties that have not been fully investigated in multifrequency bands by using the same channel sounding system. In this paper, we conduct wideband channel measurements at four frequency bands from Sub-6 GHz to 5G-Advanced (4.5, 6.5, 11, and 16 GHz) in various typical indoor scenarios via the same vector network analyzer (VNA)-based channel sounder. Channel characteristics, including path loss (PL), shadow fading (SF), and power angular delay profiles (PADP), are extracted and analyzed. Empirical models of large-scale PL and SF are proposed. In addition, the distribution of the angle of departure (AOD) and the frequency dependence of PL characteristics are studied. The result and analysis can provide realistic channel characteristics for the research on 5G-Advanced and beyond multifrequency systems.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Channel Capacity in Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Aided Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This work analyzes the capacity of the Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-aided wireless communication system deploying linear RIS. We propose modeling the cascade channel with a mixed product of random Vandermonde matrices and a random diagonal matrix. A challenging problem that has yet to be addressed is the lack of a concise and accurate expression for the capacity of this channel due to the absence of spectral properties of the Vandermonde matrix. In this paper, we tackle this problem by expressing the capacity as a series expansion and obtaining the exact moment expression of the channel covariance matrix. Simulations indicate that the derived moments provide a good prediction of the true values. The approximate expression for the channel capacity, using finite terms, is simple enough to offer valuable insights and matches the simulation results well.

articleTitle: Stochastic Geometry-Based Modelling and Analysis of Vehicular Networks: Supporting V2V and Visual Collaborative Environment Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Vision-based environment perception is a crucial component in autonomous driving technology, predominantly utilizing cameras and other visual sensors to gather information from the surrounding environment. However, the perception capability of a single vehicle is limited. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose a V2V-enabled collaborative visual environment perception framework to enhance perception accuracy and reliability of a single vehicle through information sharing and collaboration between vehicles. Particularly, we utilize the transdimensional Poisson point process (TPPP) to model the actual distribution of vehicles, where TPPP is a combination of 1D and 2D PPPs. We first derive the coverage probability of a typical vehicle located at the origin. Then, assuming that each vehicle has a reliable perception distance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>, we quantify the fraction of the mean area covered from successfully collaborating vehicles within a circular region of radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{D}$</tex> centered at the origin. It is worth noting that the metric of mean area fraction fundamentally reflects the effectiveness and performance of V2V-enabled and vision-based collaborative environmental perception. Finally, the analytical findings of this paper are validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: System Information Feedback Assisted Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Configuration: Leveraging Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a pivotal technology with considerable potential for the upcoming sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems, due to its ability to intelligently modify the characteristics of the radio environment. However, the current RIS configuration schemes, relying on perfect channel state information (CSI), are challenging to implement in practical settings. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework for RIS configuration. The proposed framework employs a straightforward system information feedback mechanism to eliminate the need for perfect CSI. Initially, we model the interaction between the RIS and the wireless communication system as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Subsequently, a RIS control scheme based on the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) method is proposed. Unlike existing works, the proposed framework effectively adapts to the dynamic changes of the wireless channels. Finally, the simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed framework offers substantial improvements over existing benchmarks.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modeling of Industrial Complex Electromagnetic Interference for IIoT
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has revolutionized industrial production. However, severe electromagnetic interference (EMI) from factory equipment presents significant challenges to industrial wireless communication, making it difficult to meet the determinism requirements. Current research primarily relies on statistical analysis, treating EMI as background noise and random pulses. This approach fails to capture and predict real-time EMI information, thus making it difficult to ensure deterministic Quality of Service (QoS) in wireless networks. Our research reveals that welding-induced EMI exhibits deterministic patterns and has a strong corrleation with industrial control instructions. Based on these findings, a modeling method is proposed that treats welding-generated EMI as a time series. Parameters were successfully extracted from measurement data, and the method's performance was effectively validated. This method demonstrates broad applicability and can be extended to measure and model EMI from various industrial production equipment. In the future, it could utilize industrial control instructions to predict real-time EMI information, facilitating efficient wireless network resource management and meeting the deterministic transmission requirements of wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Guarantee Reliable Transmission in Wireless Fading Channel for Industrial IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In industrial communications, it is imperative that critical information is transmitted without any interruptions or faults throughout the entire transmission process. Traditional communication system, however, typically focus on transmission errors at the bit level and fail to consider the time-varying characteristics of wireless channels in relation to the distribution of failures over time. In this article, we employ a classical reliability measure, i.e., Mean Time To First Failure (MTTFF), into the optimization algorithm of communication system to provide a guaranteed reliable transmission window without any errors. By exploiting the constant envelope properties of Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequences, we calculate the distribution and cumulative density function of the SNR, and accurately estimate the Level Crossing Rate (LCR), which allows us to estimate the MTTFF under current status. We then implement a optimization strategy that minimizes the transmitted power to achieve the targeted MT-TFF. Extensive experiments validates that the adjusted MTTFF achieves a satisfaction rate of more than 95%.

articleTitle: Distribution on the Pareto Boundary for Integrated Sensing and Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a promising technology for realizing beyond fifth-generation (B5G) and sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks due to its ability of significantly improving both communication and sensing performances. In this paper, we study the distribution on the performance Pareto boundary for a general ISAC scenario, a dual-functional BS simultaneously estimates the target response matrix while communicating with a user. First, we investigate the effect of randomness of random signals on sensing performance and use the lower bound of minimum mean square error (MMSE) to measure sensing performance. Then, taking the transmit signal's distribution as the optimization variable, we establish the optimization problem to realize the Pareto performance boundary. Subsequently, we show that the optimal distribution is the discrete distribution with finite mass points in single-input single-output (SISO) ISAC and discrete in amplitude and uniform in phase (DAUP) in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) ISAC. Finally, we give simulation results and provide insights into deterministic-randomness tradeoff (DRT) through analyzing changes of the distribution on the performance Pareto boundary.

articleTitle: Universal Modem Generation with Inherent Adaptability to Variant Underwater Acoustic Channels: a Data-Driven Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In underwater acoustic (UWA) communication, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is commonly employed to mitigate the inter-symbol interference (ISI) caused by delay spread. However, path-specific Doppler effects in UWA channels could result in significant inter-carrier interference (ICI) in the OFDM system. To address this problem, we introduce a multi-resolution convolutional neural network (CNN) named UWAModNet in this paper, designed to optimize the modem structure, specifically modulation and demodulation matrices. Based on a trade-off between the minimum and the average equivalent sub-channel rate, we propose an optimization criterion suitable to evaluate the performance of our learned modem. Additionally, a two-stage training strategy is developed to achieve quasi-optimal results. Simulations indicate that the learned modem outperforms zero-padded OFDM (ZP-OFDM) in terms of equivalent sub-channel rate and bit error rate, even under more severe Doppler effects during testing compared to training.

articleTitle: Multi-Scenario U6G Channel Measurement and Angular Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The upper 6 GHz (U6G) band in the frequency range of 6425–7125 MHz or even wider, has been proposed for research and application in future International Mobile Telecommunication services, which is also expected to be incorporated with the sixth-generation (6G) mobile communication system due to its capabilities of extensive coverage and wide bandwidth. In the paper, we measure and analyze the power angle spectrum (PAS) and root mean square (RMS) angular spread (AS) of the U6G channel based on the constructed multi-channel channel sounder in typical scenarios, including indoor hall, indoor corridor, outdoor and outdoor-to-indoor (O2I). Observations reveal that the PAS of the U6G channel exhibits a dominant path with several multipath components, confirming that the scattering in the U6G frequency band is limited and exhibits sparse characteristics when the line-of-sight link exists. In addition, we also verify the non-stationary characteristics of the U6G channel by analyzing the angle-domain parameters of the virtual array.

articleTitle: Cross-Channels Identification for Specific Emitters Using Global and Local Semantic Consistency
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: By analyzing and comparing features extracted from wireless signals, Specific Emitter Identification (SEI) refers to a technology that determines and distinguishes different radio devices. However, in practical applications, wireless signal transmission is affected by varying channel conditions, leading to signal changes such as multipath effects, attenuation, and interference. Furthermore, deep learning is crucial for building automated decision systems in SEI research, but its effectiveness depends on having a certain quantity of labeled training data, a resource that is often challenging and costly to acquire in new environments. This can result in a sharp decline in model performance when applied to new environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cross-channel SEI method based on semantic consistency, aiming to tackle the challenge of identification with limited labeled training samples. The method integrates island loss with domain adversarial training to extract domain-invariant features by constraining Global Semantic Consistency (GSC) and Local Semantic Consistency (LSC), thus improving recognition performance under varying channel conditions. Experiments were conducted on a data collection of 16 USRP X310 radios, and the proposed approach achieved recognition accuracies of 81.25 % in the target domain and 89.70% in the source domain with just 1% labeled modeling samples in the target domain, significantly outperforming other methods. The experimental findings show that the proposed approach exhibits excellent recognition capability in both source and target domains, achieving robust and accurate SEI even with limited labeled data.

articleTitle: FedSMW: Server-Side Model Watermark Framework for Model Ownership Verification in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has recently become a promising framework for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning, particularly under edge computing scenarios. It allows geographically dispersed devices to collaboratively train a global model under the coordination of a central server, without compromising their private data. However, as every participating local device can access the FL model, the development and deployment stages of FL are susceptible to model Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) infringement issues, including unlawful theft and misuse. Previous studies have offered schemes in which devices independently inject watermarks into the model during the local training phase to protect their IPR for the FL model. Nevertheless, this strategy may cause additional problems, such as mutual interference of watermarks, increased computational burden for distributed resource-constrained devices, and degraded global model accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework to uphold IPR in federated learning. Rather than depending on device-generated watermarks, our approach utilizes injecting watermarks from the central server, permitting it to globally and intelligently embed watermarks for every device. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our methodology can enhance the watermark injection rate and preserve main task accuracy concurrently. Furthermore, our framework can seamlessly integrate with other secure federated learning methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sliding-Correlation Frame Synchronization for Visible Light Communication with Signal- Dependent Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This work aims to analyze the effect of signaldependent noise (SDN) on sliding-correlation synchronization calculation in visible light communication. According to the data composition in the sliding-correlation window, we divide the synchronization process into three cases, and then derive the mean and variance of the correlation values in the three cases. The mean-squared error (MSE) upper bound is derived by Gaussian approximation. The simulation results show that the synchronization performance becomes better as the proportion of symbol “0” in the synchronization sequence increases. The synchronization performance can be influenced by the SDN coefficient. Finally, we present two criteria to select the synchronization sequence based on the minimization of MSE upper bound and the minimization of simulated MSE, respectively. The results of the two criteria are very close.

articleTitle: Language-Oriented Semantic Communication for Image Transmission with Fine-Tuned Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Ubiquitous image transmission in emerging applications brings huge overheads to limited wireless resources. Since that text has the characteristic of conveying a large amount of information with very little data, the transmission of the descriptive text of an image can reduce the amount of transmitted data. In this context, this paper develops a novel semantic communication framework based on a text-2-image generative model (Gen-SC). In particular, a transmitter converts the input image to textual modality data. Then the text is transmitted through a noisy channel to the receiver. The receiver then uses the received text to generate images. Additionally, to improve the robustness of text transmission over noisy channels, we designed a transformer-based text transmission codec model. Moreover, we obtained a personalized knowledge base by fine-tuning the diffusion model to meet the requirements of task-oriented transmission scenarios. Simulation results show that the proposed framework can achieve high perceptual quality with reducing the transmitted data volume by up to 99% and is robust to wireless channel noise in terms of portrait image transmission.

articleTitle: Lightweight Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding for Semantic Communications Over Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) emerges as a novel technology in semantic communication, coin-ciding with the rising demand for edge devices in the Internet of Things (IoT). Consequently, the deployment of DeepJSCC on edge devices becomes a pivotal research direction in semantic communication. However, DeepJSCC confronts issues related to the fading of complex channels. Besides, implementing DeepJSCC on edge devices also poses challenges due to the constrained computing resources. In this paper, we propose a method named DeepJSCC with Ensemble learning (DeepJSCC-ES) to enhance its ability in resisting fading in the Rician channel. Furthermore, we present a solution by introducing a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)-adaptive pruning algorithm called the DeepJSCC SNR-Adaptive Pruning method (DJSAP) to make the DeepJSCC network lightweight, reducing computational complexity and enhancing its suitability for edge devices. Our simulations show that the DeepJSCC-ES system significantly outperforms the baseline DeepJSCC, particularly excelling in low SNR conditions. Further, the parameter size of the pruned model using DJSAP is compressed by 93.37%, while the average structural similarity index metric (SSIM) for the images only decreases by 0.92% compared with the baseline DeepJSCC.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency Laser Range Finder with Coherent Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The precise range measurement is a fundamental component of reliable Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Conventional phase-shifted laser ranging architectures have been demonstrated to exhibit deterioration in modulation depth and frequency stability with increasing frequency, which leads to decreased accuracy. In this context, we propose a novel architecture for implementing a Dual-Frequency Laser Range Finder (DF-LRF) based on the phase-shift range measurement. With optical frequency modulation technology, which guarantees high frequency modulation depth and stability, a dual-frequency laser with a difference of 200MHz is obtained. As a result, the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of the backscattered signals is improved, and the ranging accuracy and detection sensitivity of the DF-LRF are enhanced. The SNR and ranging results of the DF-LRF are experimentally measured and analyzed. When the dual-frequency laser heterodyne is used in the DF-LRF, the SNR of the beat signal is improved by 3.67dB. With the aggravation of phase jitter, the absolute and relative ranging accuracy deteriorates compared with those without heterodyne in the DFLRF, which provides a reference for integrating DF-LRF into the IoT system.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning from Human-like Feedback Enhances Semantic Communication with Multimodal LLMs
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Semantic communication is an emerging intelligent paradigm that provides some special solutions for the various future applications. With the rise of large language model (LLM), it may enhance well on semantic communication. However, how to balance on the accuracy and the efficiency of compression remains an urgent issue to semantic communication with LLMs. In this paper, we design a multimodal large language models (MLLMs)-enabled semantic communication system specifically designed for image transmission, where the reinforcement learning from human-like feedback (RLHLF) framework is proposed to apply reasoning and self-reflection capabilities of MLLMs to enhance the quality of semantic extraction and image generation. For one thing, we first optimize the image semantic information at the transmitter by RLHLF framework. For another thing, the generated images are optimized at the receiver by RLHLF framework. Simulation results show that our proposed system provides bandwidth savings and enables graceful performance improvement as the channel quality improves, which proves the potential of MLLMs for future semantic communication.

articleTitle: Imperceptible Screen-Camera Communication Based on Inter-Frame Difference and Noise Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Rapid and convenient connection between digital devices is a hot topic. A practical solution is to exploit screens to transmit and cameras to receive, where high confidentiality can be achieved. In this work, we investigate an imperceptible screen-camera communication over metres, where “imperceptible” implies that the signals are transmitted without detectable features imposed on the images. We designed weights on red, green and blue channels to ensure reliability and imperceptibility. We also fully considered the manifestations of different types of noise in results of inter-frame difference and analyzed their causes and characteristics. By modeling the channel and the noise, we obtain the theoretically optimal scheme for the receiver to ensure the best error rate performance. Through experiments of photographing under different conditions, the reliability and accuracy of the novel method are validated.

articleTitle: Task-Oriented Feature Re-Encoding and Forwarding for Relay-Assisted Device-Edge Co-Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we explore a task-oriented relay strategy for enhancing classification task performance in device-edge co-inference systems. In particular, we propose a deep neural network (DNN) based Re-encoding and Forwarding (RF) strategy, whereby the relay re-encodes the extracted feature from the edge device (ED) and then delivers it to the edge server (ES) for task execution. Unlike the conventional amplify and forward (AF) strategy where the extracted feature is simply amplified and relayed in fixed dimension, RF can produce re-encoded features with flexible dimensions to maximize the inference accuracy under constrained communication resources. Simulation results show that, unlike AF, the optimal relay position of RF is no longer at the midpoint of link ED-ES. For all considered channel conditions, RF can provide up to 11.6% higher task inference accuracy over AF by jointly adjusting the relay position and the feature dimension at the relay device (RD).

articleTitle: Adversarial Attack Based-on Transferability for Specific Emitter Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deep learning model for specific emitters identification(SEI) is vulnerable to adversarial samples generated by the application of subtle perturbations. However, it is observed that gradient-based adversarial samples generated by white box are poorly effective when they transfer to attack black box. This situation creates the misleading impression that the SEI model possesses excellent robustness. In this study, we propose Virtual Model Gradient Attack (VGA) to improve the attack success rates in black box and enhance the transferability. Firstly, virtual model endows the white box with multiple decision boundaries, aiming to extract multiple gradient information from a single model. Then, VGA achieves fast convergence of the gradients and avoids the occurrence of local optima during the convergence process through the implementation of a gradient update policy. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that VGA outperforms the existing transferability-based attack algorithms, and the adversarial samples generated by VGA has excellent concealment.

articleTitle: McEliece Public-Key Cryptosystem Based on Cyclic Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The McEliece public key cryptosystem is known for its resistance to quantum attacks. However, its application potential remains limited due to challenges such as large key size and low coding efficiency. In this paper, we proposed a McEliece public-key cryptosystem based on cyclic codes to reduce the key size. The matrix generated by the Goppa codes is replaced with the matrix generated by the cyclic code in encoding, the private key matrix is transformed into the row vector of the generator polynomial. Performance evaluations and security analysis reveal that the refined system retains commendable coding efficacy and security with a condensed key space.

articleTitle: Convolutional Deep Unfolding Network for Asynchronous Active User Detection and Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Grant-free random access has garnered considerable attention in recent years. However, the absence of scheduling means user signals might arrive asynchronously at the base station. Fortunately, sporadic activity and restricted latency transform active user detection and channel estimation boils down into the sparse linear inverse problem of compressive sensing, which can be addressed by deep unfolding networks, e.g., Learned Iterative Shrinkage Thresholding Algorithm (LISTA). Nonetheless, as the maximum user delay rises, the number of training parameters escalates exponentially. To address this issue, we analyze the structural characteristics of asynchronous sensing matrices and design a convolutional network to incorporate partial structures of LISTA, ensuring that the number of training parameters does not grow with increased maximum delay. An autoencoder network for pilot optimization is investigated to fur-ther enhance the performance. Experimental results verify that the convolutional network-assisted LISTA with pilot optimization can achieve enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Detecting Diverse Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning Based on Joint Similarity
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) can combine information from multiple parties and does not require clients to upload their local privacy data, which pays a vital role in protecting privacy information of clients. However, some malicious clients exploit vulnerabilities in Federated Learning system, attempting to undermine its performance by contaminating local data or model parameter, known as poisoning. Our proposed method, Federated Learning Poisoning Defense System (FLPD), can identify potential poisoning attackers using joint similarity. Additionally, rather than directly removing the attackers, we adjust its weight and rectify its gradient. This approach not only minimizes the impact of the attackers but also leverages their gradient diversity to enhance convergence speed. We conduct experiments under multiple attack scenarios and find that our method generally achieves higher detection accuracy compared to existing approaches.

articleTitle: Routing Strategy in LEO Satellite Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite network is promising to meet the low latency, extensive coverage, and flexible networking requirements for future 6G communications. To realize efficient data transmission in dynamic LEO satellite network, an appropriate routing strategy is essential. In this paper, we investigate a multi-task LEO satellite network. Specifically, the routing strategies for all tasks are designed to maximize the quality of service (QoS) for data transmission. Since the formulated problem is a mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, a multi-agent reinforcement learning-based routing algorithm (MARL-RA) is proposed to address this problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the QoS of data transmission and reduces the end-to-end (E2E) delay by 50%, 33% and 16.7% compared to other benchmark schemes, respectively.

articleTitle: Uplink Transmission of Local RIS Data Using Orthogonal Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: We propose several uplink transmission schemes of local RIS data using two orthogonal polarizations for the array elements. The first scheme transmits 1 bit of local data per user symbol period using two simple polarization patterns. The second is a multilevel scheme that transmits 2 bits of local data per user symbol period using 4 polarization patterns. Finally, the third is a multi-dimensional scheme that transmits 3 bits of local data every two user symbol periods. Compared to the earlier local RIS data transmission schemes based on the concept of spatial modulation (RIS-SM), the proposed schemes have two fundamental advantages: First, by activating all of the RIS array elements, they do not involve any degradation in user signal performance, and second, they overcome the strong performance degradation caused by spatial correlation in RIS-SM system.

articleTitle: MicroFrame: A Multi-Complementary Color-Based Spatial Diversity System for Imperceptible and Robust Screen-Camera Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Imperceptible screen-camera communication (SCC) has garnered significant attention due to its ability to allow users to view screen content while seamlessly embedding information within the display. However, existing screen-camera communication technologies often fail to align the camera precisely without supervision, leading to incomplete information capture for decoding. In this paper, we introduce MicroFrame, a novel screen-camera communication method designed to ensure that captured content reliably includes complete information for decoding. Spatial diversity technology is employed to capture complete content. Multi-complementary color techniques are employed to enhance spectrum efficiency and maintain inconspicuous system characteristics. Experimental results demonstrate that at distances less than 1 meter, MicroFrame achieves a transmission rate of 3 kbps with over 90% Region of Interest (ROI) success rate and a Bit Error Rate (BER) on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>.

articleTitle: Amplitude Determined Pulse Counting Based Wide Dynamic Range Signal Detection for UOWC with PMT Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Photomultiplier tube (PMT) is typically employed for weak signal detection in underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) systems, which aims to further extending transmission distance. However, the intrinsic operating characteristics of PMTs are generally influenced by incident optical power. This work presents a novel signal detection structure, which consists an amplitude determined pulse counting (ADPC) method and an adaptive threshold updating process, to significantly reduce the implementation complexity and cost. The feasibility of the proposed method is experimentally verified across various PMT operating regimes, and its robustness in different conditions is discussed. Experimental results show that the proposed method effectively facilitates signal detection for a wide dynamic range of incident optical Power.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Information Preamble Multiplicity Detection in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the grant-free random access (GFRA) scenario, orthogonal preamble collisions of massive active user equipments (UEs) may lead to communication access failure. However, cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) system has good signal spatial sparsity, which can largely mitigate the interference from colliding UEs in the preamble domain. Therefore, blind detection of the preamble collision situation before formal access can provide relevant information about the preamble collision for subsequent access. This paper proposes a fully-connected neural network (FNN) based preamble multiplicity detection, specifically, to obtain information about the number of colliding UEs choosing the same preamble and the APs near the collision UEs based on the preamble energy and angle of arrival (AOA) information of the received signal. The simulation proves that preamble multiplicity detection using multidimensional information can yield reliable predictions that are significantly better than the results of detection using only one-dimensional information.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Semantic Communications for Image Transmission Over MIMO Interference Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Semantic communications offer promising prospects for enhancing data transmission efficiency. However, existing schemes have predominantly concentrated on point-to-point transmissions. In this paper, we aim to investigate the validity of this claim in interference scenarios compared to baseline approaches. Specifically, our focus is on general multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) interference channels, where we propose an interference-robust semantic communication (IRSC) scheme. This scheme involves the development of transceivers based on neural networks (NNs), which integrate channel state information (CSI) either solely at the receiver or at both transmitter and receiver ends. Moreover, we establish a composite loss function for training IRSC transceivers, along with a dynamic mechanism for updating the weights of various components in the loss function to enhance system fairness among users. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed IRSC scheme effectively learns to mitigate interference and outperforms baseline approaches, particularly in low signal-tonoise (SNR) regimes.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in A Dual-Sensor Update System for Age of Information Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This work focuses on the resource allocation in a remote monitoring system where two sensors use the zero-wait strategy to sample the same physical processes and transmit updates to the monitor. To improve the timeliness of updates, a resource allocation optimization problem is formulated to minimize the average age of information (AoI) of the system. An algorithm that seeks for the optimum is proposed. For the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime, an approximate closed-form expression for the optimal power allocation is given. In the low SNR regime, we show that the average AoI is minimized when all the power is allocated to the sensor with a large bandwidth. Moreover, we generalize the obtained results to bandwidth allocation optimization. Furthermore, the resource allocation problem is considered in a non-orthogonal multiple access case and the optimal rate pair is presented.

articleTitle: Exploring the Throughput Capacity Limits of LEO Satellite Constellation Networks: Mathematical Models and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The throughput capacity of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation networks has become increasingly significant for satisfying the high demands of future communication systems. However, the misalignment between the constellation topology and traffic distribution can lead to network congestion, negatively impacting the throughput capacity of LEO networks. To address this issue, we propose a theoretical framework that elucidates the relationship between throughput capacity and constellation parameters, aiming to identify the achievable throughput capacity upper bound in LEO networks. It is proved that the upper bound is given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{UB}=3\sqrt{2N}(W_{lx}+W_{ly})$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> represents the size of the constellation, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_{lx}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_{ly}$</tex> represent the inter- and intra-plane data rates of the inter-satellite links (ISLs), respectively. Moreover, it indicates that a constellation topology with an average path length (APL) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{L}_{min}=\sqrt{2N}/3$</tex> can closely approach the upper bound. Besides, it is shown that indiscriminately reducing the APL of the LEO network without considering traffic distribution may degrade throughput capacity.

articleTitle: Pruning Path Min-Sum Decoding Algorithm for High-Rate Non-Binary LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The fixed path Min-Sum (FMS) algorithm efficiently decodes non-binary LDPC codes with low/moderate code rates, but suffers significant performance degradation for high code rates. This paper enhances its check node (CN) update by selecting deviation paths of high reliability according to their correct probabilities and positions over the trellis of a CN. Moreover, a path pruning strategy is introduced during the CN update to reduce the complexity of path search. Analysis results indicate that the proposed pruning path Min-Sum (PMS) algorithm efficiently decodes high-rate non-binary LDPC codes.

articleTitle: UAV Complex Interference Signal Recognition Based on Lightweight Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In order to improve the complex interference signals recognition capability of UAVs, this paper proposes an efficient and accurate approach for classifying complex interference signals based on lightweight neural network. Firstly, thirteen types of different interference signals are generated. Then, these signals are transformed into time-frequency spectrum by short-time fourier transform (STFT) to construct the complex communication interference signal dataset. Finally, the MobileNetV2 lightweight neural network model is used to extract interference features and classify the interference signals. Simulation results show that compared with other interference signal recognition algorithms based on lightweight neural networks, including PPLCNetV2, ShuffleNetV2 and GhostNet, the proposed algorithm has better performance than others in terms of recognition accuracy and inference time.

articleTitle: Neural Video Compression with Dynamic Temporal Context Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Neural Video Compression (NVC) has advanced significantly in recent years, with improvements in inter-prediction techniques enabling neural video codecs to outperform traditional methods. Most NVCs rely on pixel information from neighboring frames or a single temporal feature for motion compensation, which does not fully utilize the available information on the decoder side. In this paper, we introduce an innovative and efficient motion compensation method that leverages long-term spacial-temporal dependencies in video coding and dynamically mines temporal features. Specifically, the proposed Dynamic Temporal Context Mining (DTCM) module utilize spatial information from reconstructed images to compensate for temporal features, thereby correcting errors accumulated during temporal propagation. The DTCM module extends the model's observation window, allowing for the integration of longer-term temporal information to enhance the current reference features. Additionally, the masks generated by DTCM during the prediction process act as an attention mechanism, further filtering the prediction features and enhancing the quality of the reference features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving 45.38% bitrate saving compared to the baseline approach.

articleTitle: Applications of Large-Scale Quantum Neural Networks Based on Distributed Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This research investigates the limitations of current quantum hardware in fulfilling the computational demands of quantum neural networks. It introduces an optimized circuit computed method leveraging bit splitting within the framework of distributed quantum computing. The research exemplifies this approach by decomposing a 25-qubit variational quantum circuit into several smaller 5-qubit circuits, thereby enabling distributed quantum computations. A hybrid quantum-classical neural network architecture employing this methodology was implemented and evaluated on selected computer vision datasets. The results were promising, affirming the viability of the approach. The successful implementation of this architecture suggests that future distributed quantum computing systems will likely consist of scalable, heterogeneous quantum systems interconnected through an extensive quantum network. This configuration is anticipated to significantly enhance computational power and versatility, expanding the scope of quantum computing applications in real-world scenarios. This advancement not only validates the feasibility of distributed quantum architectures but also underscores their potential to revolutionize various technological domains through enhanced computational capabilities.

articleTitle: Constructing Random QC-LDPC Codes Based on the Relationship between 8-Cycles and Trapping Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper presents a computer-aided search scheme based on simulated annealing methodology for regular quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check (QC-LDPC) codes, ensuring a minimum girth of at least 8. The approach utilizes the simulated annealing algorithm, leveraging the correlation between cycles and trapping sets, and analyzes their positioning in the Tanner graph to iteratively reduce trapping sets. This process ultimately results in the generation of high-girth QC-LDPC codes. A significant advantage of our method is that it greatly reduces the search time compared to existing approaches. Furthermore, our method generates QC-LDPC codes that demonstrate a diminution in the number of 8-cycles, concurrently achieving a reduction in detrimental trapping sets. Simulation results reveal that our method generates QC-LDPC codes with excellent bit error rate performance.

articleTitle: Satellite Transmission with Joint Source-Channel Coding Under Stochastic Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Joint source-channel coding(JSCC) is one of the AI-enabled transmission technologies that has its great potential to improve the transmission reliability. In this paper, the resource optimization problem of transmitting images via JSCC satellite communication characterized by stochastic processes is inves-tigated. An objective function that comprehensively considers both the image resolution and the information entropy of the image is constructed in the optimization problem, while latency, reconstruction quality, power constraints are simultaneously considered in the problem. Specially, user tolerance time is set as time slot to balance user tolerance and bandwidth saving. By applying the linear programming techniques, the optimization problem is effectively solved. Through various comparative tests, a practical set of parameters is devised for implementation in conclusion. Simulation results proves the effectiveness of our proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Cross-modality Deformed Footprint Image Retrieval by Shape and Multi-layer Information
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deformed of the surface can increase the modality discrepancy between barefoot footprint dust images and grayscale images. To address this issue, this paper proposes a crossmodality footprint image retrieval algorithm based on shape and multi-layer information. Firstly, a cross-modality dataset containing barefoot footprint images from 100 individuals is collected and constructed. Shape features are extracted from the footprint grayscale images to reduce the interference of deformation features, thereby minimizing the modality discrepancy between the two types of images. Then, hierarchical fusion (HF) module is further proposed to capture important information across different layers and to focus on the relationships among the toe, sole, and heel regions of the footprint, reduce the discrepancy between the two modalities under the combined constraints of ID loss, triplet loss, and center guided separation loss. Extensive experiments conducted on the footprint dataset constructed for this study demonstrate that the retrieval accuracy of the proposed method surpasses that of several other retrieval methods, showing significant promise for the comparison and identification of deformed surface footprints.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Assisted Timely Data Collection in IoT Networks with Faulty Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Thanks to their low deployment costs and high flexibility, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have been widely applied for data collection in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. However, the unpredictable status updates from deployed sensor nodes (SN) and potential failures of SN can affect the freshness of information. In this paper, we investigate the UAV data collection in monitored areas with redundant SNs to alleviate the impact of potential SN failures. The SNs generate status updates at random time slots, which will be collected by UAVs and transmitted to a data center. In order to minimize the average age of synchronization (AoS) of the network and the UAV energy consumption, we formulate a Markov decision process and adopt dueling double deep Q network (D3QN) method to optimize UAV flight trajectories. Simulation results demonstrate that our method achieves better performance compared with baseline policies in environments where SN failures occur.

articleTitle: Coded Caching with Area-Based User Combinations
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Coded caching is an effective method for alleviating traffic burden in broadcast networks by jointly optimizing caching and transmission strategies. In most previous works, users maintain isolated cache contents even when they are in close proximity. However, real-world scenarios exhibit diverse distributions of user locations, enabling low-cost content sharing among nearby users, which further reduces the network traffic. These scenarios can be modeled as a coded caching problem with area-based user combinations, where users in the same area can share cache contents. In this paper, we focus on scenarios where the number of users in each area is known during the content placement phase, referred to as the user connectivity. With the given user connectivity, we propose a decentralized coded caching transmission scheme and analyze its upper bound on the transmission rate. Additionally, the corresponding lower bound for any achievable scheme is derived. Regardless of the user connectivity, the gap between these two bounds is proved to be within a constant factor of 16. Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Explainable Machine Learning-Based Layered CSI Feedback in Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In massive MIMO system, it is important for the base station (BS) to obtain channel state information (CSI) for precoding to improve beamforming gain in frequency division duplexing (FDD) systems. One of the biggest challenges is that CSI feedback overhead is remarkably huge especially for high rank number and meanwhile significantly fluctuates with the varying rank number. The uplink(UL) resources allocation is hard to match accurately the need for CSI feedback. Recent studies show that machine learning (ML) based CSI feedback has demonstrated impressive performance gain in CSI feedback overhead reduction. However, the compressed CSI feedback bits by ML models are not explainable and can not represent any physical meaning, and thus the feedback bits can't be treated dif-ferently by discarding insignificant beam coefficiencies. Inspired by scalable video coding (SVC) and semantic communication, in order to generate layered CSI feedback bits, we propose a segment-level loss design and an iterated training strategy for ML based CSI feedback. Simulation results show that the different segments of the compressed CSI feedback bits demonstrate distinct importance weight for the CSI recovery accuracy, which brings great transmission efficiency improvement. Moreover, adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) enabled CSI segments is proposed to carry as more segments as possible and simulation results show that the CSI feedback accuracy can be improved greatly especially under relatively good SNR.

articleTitle: Reliability vs Stability: Polar Code Construction Based on Varentropy Under the Successive Cancellation List Decoding
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Successive cancellation list decoding (SCL) is a high-performance decoding algorithm designed for polar codes. To date, a comprehensive criterion for the optimal construction of polar codes under the SCL decoding remains elusive. We consider varentropy as a measure of synthetic channel stability and introduce it into the construction of polar codes under the SCL decoding. This is referred to as the RM-Var construction. The encoding of polar codes is generally dependent on the channel, while varentropy is a statistical characteristic purely based on channel transition probabilities. Introducing varentropy into the construction aligns better with the characteristics of polar codes. In certain scenarios, the RM-Var construction demonstrates superior performance compared with traditional constructions, suggesting that we may have identified a new criterion for the construction of polar codes under the SCL decoding.

articleTitle: Theoretical BER Analysis for FBMC/QAM Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Filter bank multicarrier/quadrature amplitude modulation (FBMC/QAM) with two prototype filters has been studied as an alternative waveform for post-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) wireless communications. However, the analysis of its theoretical bit error rate (BER) is still missing in the literature, which motivates our work. In this paper, it is proved that the real and imaginary parts of the intrinsic interference are identically distributed in the FBMC/QAM system, and their discrete probability density functions (PDFs) are presented. Based on these new results, the closed-form BER expressions of FBMC/QAM are derived for AWGN, flat Rayleigh and frequency-selective Rayleigh channels. Numerical results demonstrate that the derived BER expressions match perfectly with the Monte Carlo simulations, except for the high SNR region of frequency-selective channels.

articleTitle: Joint Trajectory and Resource Allocation Optimization for UAV-Assisted Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) network based on time division multiple access (TDMA) method for ground users. We propose to minimize the total energy consumption through jointly optimizing the 3D UAV trajectory, scheduling design, computation task assignment, transmission power, local and offloading computation resource allocation. To solve the problem with multiple variables, multiple non-convex constraints and non-linear and non-convex objective function, the original problem is decomposed into two subproblems using the alternating optimization, which are scheduling design and joint 3D trajectory and resource allocation optimization. Then an optimization algorithm is proposed based on successive convex approximation (SCA) method. The simulation results show that our joint scheme performances better compared with the benchmark scheme, which also confirms the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: A Cyclic Placement Strategy for Multi-Access Coded Caching
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: We investigate the multi-access coded caching problem, which involves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> files, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> users, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> caches. Each user can access <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> adjacent caches in a cyclic manner. We present a novel coded placement scheme for the case of cache size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M=\displaystyle \frac{K-1}{KL}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\displaystyle \frac{K-1}{L}$</tex> is an integer. The scheme is based on coded placement and involves cyclic placement in caches. We show that the scheme achieves a lower worst-case transmission rate than existing schemes in some cases when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\leq K-L$</tex>. As for the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N > K-L$</tex>, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N > 2,L=K-1$</tex> and cache size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M \in\left[0, \frac{1}{K}\right]$</tex>, our proposed achievable scheme is another way to achieve the optimal memory-rate tradeoff, in addition to the scheme proposed by Namboodiri and Rajan.

articleTitle: A Time Series Model for Communication Scenario Recognition with Weighted Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Wireless communication is in strong demand of high throughput, low latency and high reliability, while mobility brings challenges to these demands. In particular, dynamic communication scenarios bring difficulty to communication devices in adjusting transmission strategies accordingly. Communication scenario recognition provides specific information of the environ-ment to mobile devices to make more intelligent communication strategies. We propose a long short-term memory (LSTM)-based model called SERA, which exploits the temporal relationship between the samples of multivariate data collected by mobile devices. In the proposed model, we have designed weighted correction (WCR) as a real-time post-processing to smooth the recognition results. Furthermore, we implement extensive performance analyses and simulations to validate SERA. Our experiments with real-world data demonstrate a 20% improve-ment in recognition performance over existing benchmarks.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Spectrum Sharing for Cellular V2X Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Increasingly scarce spectrum resources prompt spectrum sharing to be quite a potential solution to improve efficiency in the scenario of cellular vehicle-to-everything (CV2X), yet the respective quality of service (QoS) of different kinds of communication links should not be overlooked or confused. Besides, in response to the demand for green communication, the energy efficiency (EE) at the system level should be taken into consideration. Therefore, an energy-efficient spectrum sharing scheme with controllable interference is proposed in this paper, focusing on reusing spectrum between two typical technologies with different QoS requirements in C-V2X, more specifically, vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) with required capacity and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) with specific reliability.
