As an algorithm to achieve the optimal solution by imitating the natural evolution, a modified genetic algorithm (GA) with infeasible solution repairing is adopted to maximize the system EE thanks to its capability to cope with complex problems and reach the global optimal solution. Simulation results show that GA obtains a satisfactory convergence and the proposed spectrum sharing scheme effectively promotes the system EE.

articleTitle: A Consensus Averaging Synchronization Algorithm for Distributed Transmit Beamforming Based on Event-Triggered Updates
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Distributed transmit beamforming technology involves the coordinated operation of multiple antenna nodes to achieve signal direction control and enhancement. This paper addresses the critical issue of frequency and phase synchronization among nodes in this technology by proposing a consensus averaging synchronization algorithm for distributed transmit beamforming based on event-triggered updates (CAS-DBET). This algorithm incorporates both signal strength and asynchrony metrics to classify transmitting nodes. For nodes with strong signals that meet the asynchrony threshold, it uses an event-triggered approach to update frequency and phase parameters. Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm improves overall synchronization efficiency and reduces synchronization time while maintaining 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> accuracy. It outperforms existing methods in terms of time complexity and scalability, making it suitable for large-scale distributed wireless systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Semantic Communication for Image Transmission over MIMO Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm through the transmission of semantic features to improve spectrum efficiency. This paper proposes an end-to-end semantic communication system for multi-task image transmission based on multi-input multi-output (MIMO) channel, which benefits from space multiplexing and higher channel capacity. First, we design a deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) scheme, which introduces an image cluster method at the transmitter based on the common semantic information among multiple images. Furthermore, to achieve semantic transmission of different clusters in the MIMO channel, a precoding scheme based on transformer is proposed, guaranteeing the receiver can correctly recover the semantic features. Finally, numerical results demonstrate that our proposed framework significantly outperforms other frameworks in terms of improving transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: A Joint Design of Hybrid Beamforming and Multi-Tap Cancellation for Full-Duplex mmWave MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a full-duplex (FD) joint hybrid beamforming architecture with multi-tap canceller (JHBF-MTC) to tackle the self-interference (SI) in the millime-ter wave (mmWave) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. The JHBF-MTC consists of digital precoder/combiner, analog beamformers and multi-tap canceller. The analog beamformers were designed utilizing angle-of-departure (AoD) and angle-of-arrival (AoA) information of mmWave channel, and the multi-tap canceller was designed by the residual SI. After that, we employed the iterative algorithm based on Lagrange multipliers to complete the optimization of the digital precoder/combiner. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed JHBF-MTC system significantly improves achievable sum rate and self-interference cancellation (SIC).

articleTitle: An Unequal Error Protection Scheme for Neural Network Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As artificial intelligence progresses, neural networks are widely used these days. For parameters of neural network models, bit errors occurred during transmission or storage can significantly impact the overall model performance. Given the vast number of parameters in neural networks, it requires numerous coding redundancy overhead to protect the model parameters. Consequently, identifying an effective error protection scheme to protect model parameters with less coding redundancy is crucial. To this end, we design an unequal error protection scheme to protect neural network parameters. We provide efficient protection for model parameters by designing importance-based bit grouping method according to bit error sensitivity. Then for bit groups, we develop an algorithm with reinforcement learning to determine the precise coding redundancy allocation automatically. In comparison to the existing work, our method can maintain the original model performance while using fewer coding redundancy bits.

articleTitle: Fresnel Zones Modeling and Analysis of Motion Detection for Multi-Antenna ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) based sensing approaches have unique advantages for motion detection. However, due to the introduction of additional angle information in multi-antenna system, the mapping relationship between channel gain and motion state is changed in the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scenario, which will affect the sensing performance. In this paper, we first characterize a multi-antenna Fresnel zones model that establishes a mapping relationship between the target motion parameters and channel gain. Then, we reveal that the motion state of sensing target is affected by both the path length and angle of arrival (AoA). Moreover, the analytic expressions of variation of channel amplitude related to path length and AoA are obtained. Finally, numerical results corroborate the theoretical analysis and hardware system shows the proposed sensing model can effectively detect the motion state of sensing target.

articleTitle: Game-Theoretic Deep Reinforcement Learning for Task Offloading in Heterogeneous MEC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The emergence of new applications has increased the demand of mobile users for edge computing. Therefore, the optimization of base station load balancing and task offloading is particularly important. In this paper, a two-tier heterogeneous mobile edge computing (MEC) system based on Stackelberg Game (SG) is studied. The introduction of SG can improve user association flexibility while reducing base station load. The introduction of network slicing can classify users according to different types, which increases the universality of the proposed framework. To solve the above problem, we map an optimization problem of efficiency, computation delay and computation energy consumption. Due to the non-convexity of the optimization problem, the Multi-agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm based on SG is proposed in this paper. The gradient descent strategy can converge faster and obtain the optimal solution of user association policy and unload policy. Through simulation, it is verified that the proposed scheme can obtain lower computation delay and computation energy consumption on the basis of solving the problem of base station overload.

articleTitle: Plane Wave Generator Design for Base Station Testing at FR3
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Plane wave generator (PWG) generates high-quality plane waves in quiet zone (QZ) by optimizing the excitation weight vector, achieving over-the-air (OTA) testing of the device under test (DUT) at a small distance. It becomes challenging to test DUT in far-field (FF) range with the increase of frequency and the application of massive antenna arrays. PWG has aroused widespread interest in achieving FF testing conditions for DUT at very small distances. In this paper, we design a PWG for base station testing at frequency range 3 (FR3) and analyze the impact of different element layouts. Three frequency points within FR3 are selected for PWG design and the quality of plane waves within QZ is analyzed in detail. The amplitude ripple and phase ripple are of PWGs are 0.59dB and 8.67°, 0.6dB and 8.5°, 0.67dB and 7.94° at 8GHz, 16GHz, 24 GHz, respectively, which satisfy the requirements of PWG design.

articleTitle: Design of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes with Girth at Least 8
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes are a special type of sparse graph codes that have recently attracted great interest due to their capacity-approaching performance. To reduce the performance loss in-curred by short cycles, this paper proposes a method based on the greatest common divisor (GCD) full-length row-multiplier (FLRM) matrix to construct girth-8 quasi-cyclic SC-LDPC codes with improved performance and flexible code rates. Besides, we further extend the lower bound of the circulant permutation matrix (CPM) size to be compatible with different code lengths. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed SC-LDPC code has performance gains of 1.05 dB and 1.0 dB compared with that based on RS structure at an BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>over AWGN channels for code rates 0.45 and 0.625, respectively. Additionally, SC-LDPC codes based on the GCD constraint achieve the trade-off between decoding performance and complexity..

articleTitle: Refined Parity-Check Polar Codes from PAC Codes with Lower Complexity
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As any polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) code can be transformed into a parity-check (PC) polar code with the same set of codewords, this paper proposes a new approach for refining PC-Polar codes derived from PAC codes. This approach refines PC-polar codes with simpler PC functions, which makes the decoding more efficient. For successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding of the derived PC-Polar code, we first show that its decoding performance is insensitive to the positions of information bits akin to any PC function if the degree profile of PC functions keeps unchanged. Then, we propose to employ a contiguous use of information bit positions for any PC function. For various short PAC codes, simulation results show that the refined PC-Polar code performs very close to the derived PC-Polar code under SCL decoding, but with a lower complexity in both encoding and decoding.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Multi-RIS-Aided Fluid Antenna Systems Under Nakagami-$m$ Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Recognizing the vast potential of combining reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) with fluid antenna system (FAS), we study the communication performance of multi-RIS-aided FAS under Nakagami-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> fading channels. Specifically, in the presence of a direct link, a base station with fixed single-antenna transmits information through multi-RIS to a user with FAS to aid communication. Considering the correlation among the ports of FAS, we first obtain that the equivalent channel gains for different ports obey the gamma distribution and are correlated. Then, we derive the joint cumulative distribution function of the correlated equivalent channel gain and the outage probability of the system by using the Archimedean copulas functions cluster. Finally, numerical results not only indicate that in multi-RIS-aided wireless networks, FAS can significantly improve the outage performance compared to traditional antenna systems, but also reveal that spatially correlated copula structures have a significant impact on outage performance.

articleTitle: A Fully-Automated Paper ECG Digitisation Algorithm for e-Health Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an important non-invasive tool for diagnosing heart and cardiovascular diseases. However, traditional ECG systems often provide images, which makes it challenging to directly utilize the image-based data in various applications that require 1-D signals. Therefore, the digitalization of ECG reports is essential for the establishment of electronic medical archives, advanced diagnostic tools, and intelligent healthcare systems. Previous efforts to digitize paper-based ECGs have been limited by the need to manually select regions of interest, limited accuracy in handling overlapping ECG leads, and lack of batch processing capabilities. We present a fully automated method for digitizing ECG reports that requires only a predefined lead distribution, eliminating the need for manual lead position selection. This method effectively addresses the challenge of overlapping leads and has the capability for automated batch processing. Validation against a subset of the PTB-XL dataset demonstrated high accuracy and reliability (Root Mean Square Error: 0.036 (mV), Pearson Correlation Coefficient: 0.977). To further verify the generalizability of the method, we applied the algorithm to hospital ECG reports. The results, evaluated by expert cardiologists, confirmed that our method produced consistently high-quality digitalization and demonstrated its applicability to different types of ECG reports.

articleTitle: An Interference Mitigation Method via Variable Separation Angle between LEO Constellations
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With a large number of satellites in orbit, there is an inevitable problem of co-frequency interference between low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations. However, existing studies tend to focus on avoidance strategies with a constant angle, ignoring the positional relationship between satellites and earth stations. In this paper, our work is to study the interference mitigation strategy between LEO constellations and propose a variable separation angle method based on different positional relationships while selecting the optimal separation angle in each case. Moreover, given the satellite capacity, the joint optimal problem of minimum separation angle and maximum channel capacity is established and solved by the whale optimization algorithm (WOA) for its better convergence speed and stability with respect to other algorithms. Meanwhile, the separation angle strategy is applied to interference simulation based on Oneweb and Lightspeed. Compared to the fixed separation angle strategy, the simulation results prove the method improves the system performance in terms of interference power, information rate, and interference time.

articleTitle: Indoor Measurements and Analysis at 13 GHz with a Massive SIMO Channel Sounder
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The advancement and improvement of 6G technology heavily rely on identifying and studying new frequency bands. The 13 GHz band, in comparison to existing bands, offers higher data rates, lower latency, and increased capacity, thus meeting the more rigorous network performance requirements of future applications. This paper utilizes channel measurement techniques with a large-scale single-input multiple-output (SIMO) channel sounder to conduct indoor measurements at 13 GHz. The data analysis investigates the wireless channel characteristics of indoor environments at the 13 GHz band. The evaluation of specific parameters includes the power delay profile, delay spread, angular spread, and spatial consistency in both Line-of-Sight (LOS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) scenarios. Unlike LOS scenarios, the measurement points in NLOS scenarios exhibit more complex multipath components, greater delay spread and angular spread, and lower signal-to-noise ratios. Moreover, by analyzing the angles and power of radial and tangential paths of the measurement points, the spatial consistency of the 13 GHz indoor channel is validated.

articleTitle: LDA-Based Signal Detection Method for Underwater Optical Wireless Communication System With PMT Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To address the issues in existing signal detection methods, this work proposes a linear discriminant analysis (LDA)-based signal detection method for underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) system with photo-multiplier tube (PMT) receiver. The proposed method adopts LDA to acquire the optimal projection vector for the combination of received signal samples. To further reduce the computational complexity, simplification is performed in the calculation of the projection vector based on the correlation analysis of PMT output samples. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method yields better bit error rate (BER) performance than the benchmark methods. Specifically, the proposed method achieves an optical power gain of at least 2 dB over the benchmark methods at the BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–3</sup> with 4-time sampling under dynamic channel.

articleTitle: Robust Semantic Communication System for Image Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust semantic communication system. Initially, the sender extracts the skeleton map from the transmitted image. The coordinates of the skeleton points are then subjected. In this process, the coordinates of important semantic information are transmitted with higher power, while less important coordinates are sent with lower power. The modulated coordinates are transmitted through a Gaussian white noise channel. At the receiver, a demodulator restores the skeleton map, and a conditional diffusion model is used to reconstruct the image. Compared to transmitting entire images, transmitting only the coordinates of skeleton points significantly saves band-width. The non-uniform modulation protects critical semantic information, enhancing robustness. Experimental results show that this method reduces the volume of the transmission data from 180kbits to just 5bits. The compression rate is around 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>. In low SNR environments, the PSNR curve steadily increases as the SNR increases, demonstrating the robustness of the system. Our code is available at https://github.com/agougougoua/RSCT.

articleTitle: DisenCB: Learning Diverse Disentangled Representation for Cross-Domain Consecutive Footprint Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cross-domain consecutive footprint retrieval is crucial for security screening in the security fields, which faces the challenges of large intra-class differences and mining of temporal information. This paper propose a cross-domain consecutive footprint retrieval network based on diverse disentangled representation, mining more discriminative footprint features and domain-invariant temporal information. First, we separate the footprint features into domain-relevant and domain-irrelevant features by the disentangled module; second, we introduce a complementary attention fusion module that effectively interacts domain-relevant and domain-irrelevant features to obtain a more robust feature representation; finally, the bi-directional temporal enhancement module makes full use of domain-irrelevant features while taking into account both forward and backward frame information. Experiments show that the network proposed in this paper obtains 77.78% Rank-1 on the CDSPF-200 dataset, which outperforms other retrieval networks.

articleTitle: Joint Target Estimation, Channel Estimation, and Symbol Detection for ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Interference mitigation for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is important for guaranteeing both communication and sensing performances. To suppress the interference between the downlink sensing and the uplink communication, it is necessary to judiciously design the receiver at the base station (BS). In this paper, we develop an ISAC receiver design by formulating a joint target estimation, channel estimation, and symbol detection (JEED) problem based on the maximum a posteriori (MAP) criterion, which turns out to be a mixed-integer problem. To solve this difficult problem, we develop an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm, which has fast convergence and only involves closed-form expression calculations in each iteration. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm can achieve excellent performances in terms of communication bit error rate (BER) and target sensing accuracy.

articleTitle: Joint Symbol-Level Precoding and Antenna Selection Optimization for Multiuser MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Symbol-level precoding (SLP) is an advanced technique designed to mitigate multi-user interference (MUI) and enhance transmission gain. This paper explores joint optimization of SLP and antenna selection to address the challenges of MUI and minimize the total system power consumption. The inherently non-convex optimization problem is approximated and refined to a convex one based on sparse estimation and sparse correction. We further reduce the number of constraints in the problem by introducing new circular constraints to replace the typical rectangular constraints. Subsequently, a coordinate descent (CD)-based iterative optimization algorithm is developed to solve the problem with a low complexity. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Low-Latency High-Throughput Decoder of QC-LDPC Codes by Matrix Splitting
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As the continuously increasing demand of high data rate and lower transmission, many modern communication systems employ the LDPC coding scheme with ultra-high throughput decoder to achieve these challenging requirements. However, due to the implementation complexity of decoding algorithm, designing an ultra-high throughput decoder of LDPC codes still suffers many difficulties. Therefore, we propose a FPGA-based LDPC decoder with partial parallel decoding, which splits and virtually supplements the parity-check matrix to achieve higher throughput and lower latency. Our proposed FPGA-based decoder can achieve a throughput of 6.072Gbps in 10 iterations for the highest rate 5G-LDPC code.

articleTitle: Fast Fractional Programming for Multi-Cell Integrated Sensing and Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper concerns the coordinate multi-cell beamforming design for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). The optimization objective is to maximize a weighted sum of the communication rates and the sensing Fisher information. The conventional beamforming method for massive multiple-input multiple-output transmission, i.e., the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithm, has a natural extension to the ISAC problem scenario from a fractional programming (FP) perspective. However, the extended WMMSE algorithm requires computing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \times N$</tex> matrix inverse extensively, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> is proportional to the antenna array size, so the algorithm becomes quite costly when antennas are massively deployed. To address this issue, we develop a nonhomogeneous bound and use it in conjunction with the FP technique to solve the ISAC beamforming problem without the need to invert any large matrices. It is further shown that the resulting new FP algorithm has an intimate connection with gradient projection, based on which the convergence can be accelerated.

articleTitle: Distributed Deep Convolutional Network: A Generalized SVD Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of distributed systems technology, deep learning-based methods have become a common scheme to implement multiple data processing. This paper presents a novel multi-channel encoder-decoder architecture (called as D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CN), which is explained by integrating generalized singular value decomposition (GSVD) with the principles of Hankel convolution framelet. Specifically, we employ the feature extraction capability of GSVD to perform data interactions by forward/backward propagation, where numerous inputs are designed using the common bases and the reliable performance is achieved by training shared right bases. The network intuitively shows the interactions of multiple data in propagation, which is suitable for a wide range of inverse problems. Finally, we demonstrate the superiority of D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CN over other fundamental networks through numerical experiments conducted on inverse problem tasks.

articleTitle: Sensing-Assisted Orbital-Angular-Momentum Communications for Anti-Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Wireless communications are vulnerable to jamming attacks due to their open and broadcast nature. Conventional frequency hopping techniques have poor performance under co-frequency jamming attacks, so efficient anti-jamming techniques are required to significantly improve the performance of wireless communications. In this paper, we propose the sensing-assisted orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) antijamming communications scheme, where the transmitter can simultaneously receive the jamming signals to estimate the jammer's position and send the useful signals carried by different orthogonal modes to the receiver, to significantly increase the spectrum efficiency (SE) of wireless communications under hostile jamming. To obtain the jammer's position, we develop the joint enhanced multiple signal classification and received signal strength scheme. Then, we design the mode selection scheme with optimal power allocation for anti-jamming based on the estimated jamming channel state information and the orthogonality of modes. Numerical results have shown that our proposed scheme can significantly resist hostile jamming.

articleTitle: LEO Satellite Constellation Design for Regional Coverage Based on Beam Hopping
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we design a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation for the demand of China's regional aviation and maritime coverage. Based on real data and stochastic geometry theory, we model the aviation and maritime communication requirements with H3 grid. Combining beam hopping technology and Walker Delta configuration, we design the system model consisting of the LEO satellite-aviation and maritime (A&M) network. Then, we propose an integer optimization problem to minimize the number of satellites. Considering the nonlinear effect of the satellite number on the constellation coverage capability, we design an integer search algorithm based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) to solve the problem. Simulation results indicate the advantage of beam hopping technology for saving system capacity and the influence of bandwidth and beam resources on reducing the number of satellites. Based on the results, we find that the optimal altitude of satellites is determined by the beam capacity, and the optimal inclination should lean the communication resources to latitudes with high traffic.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning of Rechargeable UAVs for AoS Minimization in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Freshness of information is a critical issue for real-time Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), due to their high flexibility and low cost, are widely deployed in time-sensitive IoT scenarios. In this article, we explore the trajectory planning problem in rechargeable-UAV-aided IoT Networks. To accurately measure the freshness of information, we introduce Age of Information (AoI) and Age of Synchronization (AoS). AoI is utilized to plan the UAVs' trajectories for accessing sensors (SNs) and reduce the average AoS of the system. UAVs can recharge at charging stations to maintain energy above a certain threshold. We formulate a Markov decision process with the objective of minimizing the average AoS under the energy constraint. To adjust the dynamic environment, we propose a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning method to jointly optimize the UAVs' flight trajectories and battery recharging. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can significantly reduce the total average AoS under the energy constraint.

articleTitle: Optimizing Handovers in Integrated 5G UAV Networks: A Core-RAN Co-location Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication has emerged as a crucial solution to meet the growing demands for user access and diverse service scenarios, extending ground access capabilities. UAVs with both the core network and Radio Access Network (RAN) offer flexible networking capabilities but experience larger handover latency. This paper addresses these issues by proposing an innovative handover procedure. Our approach introduces two key innovations: a simplified handover procedure based on User Equipment (UE) context synchronization, and a virtual user scheme to mitigate service interruptions during handovers on the data plane. We conduct a comprehensive comparison with handover processes in commercial core networks to validate our proposed scheme. The results demonstrate that our solution effectively supports user handovers in UAV networks, achieving significantly lower handover latency while ensuring continuous service reachability.

articleTitle: Variable-Length XP-HARQ for URLLC
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A variable-length cross-packet hybrid automatic repeat request (VL-XP-HARQ) is proposed to accommodate ultrareliable low-latency communications (URLLC). The spectral efficiency (SE) is firstly derived in terms of the outage probabilities, with which the SE is proved to be upper bounded by the ergodic capacity (EC). Moreover, to facilitate the maximization of the SE, the asymptotic outage probability is obtained at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with which the SE is maximized by properly choosing the number of new information bits while guaranteeing outage requirement. By applying Dinkelbach's transform, the fractional objective function is transformed into a subtraction form, which can be decomposed into multiple sub-problems through alternating optimization. By noticing that the asymptotic outage probability is a convex function, each sub-problem can be easily relaxed to a convex problem by adopting successive convex approximation (SCA). Finally, numerical results are presented for verification.

articleTitle: Deep Mean-Kernel Learning for Bayesian Optimization in IoT-Enabled Data Center
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In efforts to mitigate energy consumption in large data centers, numerous optimization strategies have been explored. However, these methods often encounter challenges including prolonged optimization times and settling on local optima. Among diverse algorithms, Bayesian optimization (BO) demonstrates exceptional performance. Due to the slow convergence and limited scalability of existing Bayesian methods in handling high-dimensional data, we explore the influence of the surrogate model on BO, and introduce an innovative optimization approach deep mean-kernel learning, which can converge rapidly to the global optimal solution in high dimensional space and is specifically designed for the refrigeration systems of data centers. In our approach, a neural network is employed to approximate the conventional mean function, while an infinite-width neural network serves as the kernel function, modifying the Gaussian process. Utilizing two prevalent acquisition functions, we conduct comparative experiments of our algorithm against existing optimization methods in the context of data center scenarios. Our findings demonstrate that our approach adeptly manages high-dimensional data and exhibits rapid convergence towards the global optima.

articleTitle: Fisher-Robust Information Bottleneck for Task-Oriented Communication with Noisy Data
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider task-oriented commu-nication for edge AI inference, where the edge device extracts features from input data with potential noise and then transmits the encoded representations to the edge server over the physical channel for inference tasks. However, it remains an open problem to balance the tradeoff between inference accuracy and robustness in the presence of both data noise and channel noise. To address this issue, we propose a robust encoding framework for task-oriented communication, named Dual-Robust Encoding (DRE), where a robust encoding framework is developed, named Fisher-Robust Information Bottleneck (FR-IB), to balance the tradeoff between relevance and robustness. We derive a tractable variational upper bound of the FR-IB objective function using the variational approximation to overcome the computational intractability of mutual information. Experiments on image classification tasks demonstrate that DRE outperforms baseline methods, showing improved robustness to data and channel variations.

articleTitle: Uplink Performance of Stacked Intelligent Metasurface-enhanced Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) stands as a key technological advancement poised to shape the forthcoming sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, the 6G demand for higher spectral and energy efficiency presents significant challenges to CF systems. To address this issue, we introduce stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) to the CF mMIMO system. Specifically, we investigate the uplink performance of a spatially correlated SIM-enhanced CF mMIMO system. The local minimum mean squared error (L-MMSE)/maximum ratio (MR) combining are adopted at the APs and the closed-form expression for uplink spectral efficiency (SE) is obtained by using two-stage signal processing. Monte-Carlo simulations are employed to validate the accuracy of the derived analytical results. The results indicate that augmenting the number of meta-atoms per layer in the SIM consistently yields improvements. Interestingly, when the number of SIM meta-atoms is small, the increase in the number of the SIM metasurface layers results in a decrease in system performance. Furthermore, the deployment of SIMs equipped with extensive meta-atoms can function as an alternative to AP antennas even without phase shift design, contributing to the robustness of system performance.

articleTitle: LASA: A Line Anchor Self-Assigned Network for Rail Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Rail detection is a critical component of railway anomaly detection systems. However, the visibility of rails in images can be significantly affected by factors such as lighting conditions, rail intersections, and vegetation coverage, making the task of accurate rail detection a considerable challenge. To solve the above problems, we propose a Line Anchor Self-Assigned Network for rail detection. This network achieves self-assigned of line anchors by adaptively adjusting their parameters multiple times, thereby improving detection performance. Specifically, our method designs a Layer Aggregation Module to align and aggregate multi-scale semantic features extracted from the backbone network and establish global long-range dependencies. The Self-Assigned Module then adaptively adjust line anchor parameters multiple times to allocate line anchors based on aggregation features. These allocated line anchors are used to accurately fit the rail instances. Additionally, to handle scenes with low visibility and occlusion, we propose Rail Contrastive Learning. This module combines locally extracted features with globally captured cross-similarity features to achieve accurate rail detection. To evaluate the effectiveness of our method, we conducted extensive experiments on a self-built database called RDD, which contains 15000 images of railway in different scenarios. The experimental results show that our method has achieved state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Digital Nonlinear Distortion Compensation for Rydberg Atomic Receiver with Quadrature Amplitude Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the advancement of quantum physics and deeper exploration of atomic systems, the integration of atoms into communication systems has garnered significant attention. Among these efforts, the use of Rydberg atoms as a communication receiver has emerged as a prominent area of research. In this work, we introduce a new mathematical modeling approach to more accurately establish the input-output relationship of a Rydberg atomic receiver. We categorize this relationship into three segments: one linear region and two nonlinear regions, facilitating a comprehensive analysis of the nonlinear challenges associated with Rydberg atomic receiver. Our findings indicate that adjusting the Rabi oscillation frequency of the coupling laser can effectively extend the linear operating range of the receiver. Furthermore, focusing on complex quadrature amplitude modulation, we propose a digital nonlinear distortion compensation method specifically designed for Rydberg atomic receiver. This method demonstrates a significant improvement in performance, enhancing the demodulation bit error rate compared to conventional linearization techniques.

articleTitle: Semantics Guided Diffusion for Deep Joint Source and Channel Coding Design
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) offers a promising avenue for enhancing transmission efficiency, especially as traditional bit-level communication approaches its theoretical limits. A key enabling technology in SemCom is deep learning-based joint source and channel coding (DeepJSCC). However, existing DeepJSCC methods lack interpretability because they transmit semantic information implicitly by mapping data to latent features. Additionally, the black-box nature of neural networks makes it challenging to ensure the reliable transmission of critical semantics. To address these challenges, we propose advancing DeepJSCC towards a more “semantic” approach. Specifically, we suggest transmitting interpretable and lightweight semantics as side information alongside JSCC latent features. At the receiver end, we introduce a novel latent diffusion model designed for wireless communication, trained from scratch to integrate seamlessly with DeepJSCC. Using the semantic side information, the receiver employs the proposed semantics-guided latent diffusion for denoising. Furthermore, since accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential in practice, we propose estimating CSI directly from the channel output. The estimated CSI is then used for step matching in the denoising diffusion process, enabling CSI-free transmission. Finally, the denoised feature is fed into the JSCC decoder to reconstruct the image. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed scheme can achieve comparable performance without accurate CSI. Additionally, guided by semantic information and leveraging the powerful diffusion model, our method surpasses current DeepJSCC schemes, delivering satisfactory reconstruction performance even at SNR = −5dB. This proposed scheme highlights the potential of incorporating diffusion models in future SemCom systems and suggests several promising applications.

articleTitle: STAR-RIS and UAV Combination for Simultaneous Task Offloading and Communications in MEC Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This study investigates a simultaneous tasks of-floading and communications (STOC) strategy in mobile edge computing (MEC) networks, facilitated by the integration of simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Diverging from conventional MEC approaches, the newly proposed scheme simultaneously accounts for the computational and communicative capacities of MEC networks, rendering it a more pragmatic solution in practice. An optimization problem is devised to maximize the weighted sum of the minimum offloaded task data and communication data, while ensuring the quality of service (QoS) constraints for STOC through joint design of time scheduling, resource allocation, active and passive beamforming, alongside with the UAV trajectory planning. A novel alternating optimization method is proposed to solve this non-convex problem with strong couplings among variables. We provide sufficient numerical results to validate the effectiveness of the proposed STOC scheme.

articleTitle: BULLET: A Fast and Lightweight End-to-End Neural Network for Joint Acoustic Echo Cancellation and Noise Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) and noise suppression (NS) are critical components in modern full-duplex real-time communication systems. Traditionally, these tasks are handled separately using large network, posing challenges for simultaneous deployment on mobile devices due to high computational demands. In this paper, we present Bullet, a lightweight end-to-end model designed to address both AEC and NS tasks. We leverage the shared features between AEC and NS, integrating both tasks into a single network to reduce computational complexity. Band Merge (BM) is used to further reduce complexity by compressing less perceptible high-frequency information, achieving a 46.9% reduction in computational load without compromising performance. To further improve the model's performance, our model incorporates perceptual loss and a Complex Ratio Masking (CRM) module, enhancing subjective quality. We design extensive data augmentation techniques to improve generalization across a variety of real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that Bullet with only 0.19M parameters achieves real-time inference on a single thread of an Intel Core i7-12700H @2.3GHz CPU, with a real-time factor (RTF) of 0.025, while maintaining competitive performance. Moreover, Bullet has been successfully deployed on actual mobile devices such as laptops and smartphones with minimal power consumption.

articleTitle: Joint Computation Offloading and Multi-User Scheduling for Max-Latency Minimization in MEC-Aided Cell-Free Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Combining cell-free networks and mobile edge computing (MEC) is expected to meet the low latency and multi-user access requirements of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). Firstly, this paper considers MEC-aided cell-free networks in multi-user access scenarios, our goal is minimizing the maximum user latency. Secondly, in order to mitigate the impact of both multi-user interference and pilot contamination on system performance, we divide the frequency band into multiple sub-channels and dynamically schedule users on sub-channels in the uplink. Subsequently, we jointly optimize computation offloading, multi-scheduling and computational resources allocation, resulting in a complex non-convex optimization problem. Finally, To address this problem, we introduce a Bisection Search Feasibility (BSF)-Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, PPO algorithm is utilized to determine user scheduling strategy, and then the remaining non-convex problem is converted into a convex opti-mization problem using BSF algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that the suggested algorithm achieves rapid convergence and surpasses the performance of baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Signal Quality Aware Deep RF Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio Frequency (RF) sensing with deep learning is evolving rapidly, resulting in numerous task networks that enable various applications. However, the notable noise and interference in RF sensing lead to variations in signal quality. If not handled properly, the low-quality signals can undermine the efficacy of task networks. In this paper, we propose a signal quality aware deep RF sensing framework to quantify the signal quality and incorporate it for performance enhancement. Specifically, we design a unified plug-in module for classic task networks which projects signal quality-related representations to quality scores and dynamically modulates the training loss of our framework to avoid the impact of low-quality signals. A novel training strategy is also developed to jointly optimize quality scores and task networks. The experiment results show our framework effectively mitigates low-quality signal interference during training. For two typical RF sensing tasks, compared to ignoring signal quality, task network performance improved by 4.2% to 5.9%.

articleTitle: FSOS-AMC: Few-Shot Open-Set Learning for Automatic Modulation Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is essential for the advancement and efficiency of future wireless commu-nication networks. Deep learning (DL)-based AMC frameworks have garnered extensive attention for their impressive classification performance. However, existing DL-based AMC frameworks rely on two assumptions, large-scale training data and the same class pool between the training and testing data, which are not suitable for few-shot and open-set scenarios. To address this issue, a novel few-shot open-set automatic modulation classification (FSOS-AMC) framework is proposed by exploiting a multi-scale attention network, meta-prototype training, and a modular open-set classifier. The multi-scale attention network is used to extract the features from the input signal, the meta-prototype training is adopted to train the feature extractor and the modular open-set classifier can be utilized to classify the testing data into one of the known modulations or potential unknown modulations. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FSOS-AMC framework can achieve higher classification accuracy than the state-of-the-art methods for known modulations and unknown modulations in terms of accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Moreover, the performance of the proposed FSOS-AMC framework under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions is much better than the compared schemes.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation-Based Low-Rate Image Communication With Diffusion Models
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Semantic communication aims to transmit the underlying semantic information of a signal from the sender to the receiver, where the key requirement is to ensure that the receiver reconstructs a signal semantically (almost) equivalent to the source. Conventional image communication methods lack effective mechanisms for preserving both semantic coherence and reconstruction quality, especially for low-rate scenarios. In this paper, we propose an alternative method, namely Instance-Consistent Image Communication (ICIC), for semantic segmentation-based low-rate image communication. Our method leverages segmented instances and detected captions as intermediate vehicles to transmit semantic information from the sender to the receiver. Once transmitted, the receiver is capable of utilizing the vehicles to regenerate images with off-the-shelf diffusion models. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, experimental results on the COCO dataset illustrate that our method obtains higher semantic accuracy and higher image quality at extremely low rates.

articleTitle: QRFPose: Query-Based 3D Pose Estimation using Radio Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The major challenge for radio-frequency-based (RF) multi-person pose estimation is to solve the problem of the global information-sparsity and local information-dense in RF signals. Unlike the visual image that the human body is located in a determined region, the majority of information regarding the human body in RF signals is concentrated in localized areas, with a small portion dispersed across global regions. However, the existing works directly follow the divide-and-conquer strategy to detect candidate regions where people may exist, and then zoom into each local region to generate human skeletons, while the information beyond local information-dense regions is ignored resulting in performance degradation. To resolve the problem, we propose a novel query-based multi-person pose estimation framework, QRFPose, to view body joints as learnable query embeddings to adaptively focus on features related to target skeleton joints. Moreover, QRFPose is carefully designed to take the geometric prior of horizontal and vertical RF signals into consideration. By leveraging the projective deformable attention rather than the naive global attention mechanism, QRFPose works more efficiently. The experimental results show that QRFPose plays favorably against state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Communication Efficiency of Summation Over a Two-Layer Quantum MAC
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To compute a summation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Sigma)$</tex> of independent classical data streams from multiple servers over a quantum multiple access channel (QMAC), every server must directly send its quantum system containing multiple qudits to the user. Previous work <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma$</tex> -QMAC in [1] considers that the servers are entangled. In this work, the maximum rate, defined as the maximum number of dits of the sum computed per qudit transmitted, is derived, and a quantum coding scheme is designed to achieve it. In practice, a server is not always directly connected to the user, necessitating a relay between them for connectivity. Motivated by this, we consider a two-layer quantum MAC (2QMAC) model, where a user is connected to a layer of mirrors, and one of the mirrors (acting as a relay) is connected to a layer of servers. Quantum systems within the same layer are entangled, whereas quantum systems across different layers are independent. In <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma-2\text{QMAC}$</tex>, deriving the maximum rates of two layers simultaneously is challenging since the rates of the two layers affect each other. To address this, we first derive the maximum rate of the first layer by neglecting the second layer. Second, to relate the rates of the two layers, we derive the maximum rate of the second layer for a given feasible rate (less than the maximum rate) of the first layer. In addition, a joint coding scheme based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-sum box abstraction is designed to achieve the maximum rate of the second layer.

articleTitle: An Efficient Cluster-Based Asynchronous Activity Detection Algorithm for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient cluster-based activity detection algorithm for asynchronous grant-free random access (GFRA) cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. To address the uncertain delay challenge in the asynchronous transmission scenario, we aim to enhance the accuracy of active user devices detection and meanwhile reducing the computational complexity of the detection process by utilizing an efficient cluster-based block coordinate descent (BCD) activity detection algorithm. This challenge is heightened in the context of ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), where precise and timely detection of active users is crucial. To enhance the efficiency of the detection process, we investigate an active set strategy to reduce the number of potential active user devices requiring identification. The accuracy of active user device detection for asynchronous GFRA in CF-mMIMO systems is significantly enhanced by the implementation of the proposed cluster-based BCD algorithm with active set. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior detection performance with lower computational complexity compared to the traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Reflecting Surface Can Be A Passive Anchor to Localize Near-Field and Far-Field Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper considers a bi-static localization archi-tecture in the sixth-generation (6G) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) network, where a single-antenna user emits orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals in the uplink, and a multi-antenna base station hears the echo signals from the targets to localize them. In particular, we focus on a challenging scenario where the line-of-sight (LOS) paths between the targets and the BS are blocked such that it is impossible to estimate the propagation delay and the angle-of-arrival (AOA) information of the targets regarding to the BS as in the conventional bi-static radar system. This paper proposes to leverage the intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) as a passive anchor to tackle the above challenge. Specifically, an IRS is deployed at a proper site with LOS paths to the targets such that the distance and AOA information of the targets regarding to the IRS is embedded in the signals received by the BS over the user-target-IRS-BS path. Moreover, an efficient signal processing method is devised such that based on the signals received by the BS, we can 1. detect which targets are in the far-field region and which are in the near-field region of the IRS; 2. estimate the distance and AOA information regarding to the IRS so as to perform localization. Numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness of our proposed IRS-aided localization scheme exploiting IRS as a passive anchor for localization purpose.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enables Uplink Interference Suppression in RIS-Aided Proactive Mobile Network
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The proactive mobile network (PMN) is an innovative architecture to support minimal latency communications. It adopts an open-loop communication mode, which cancels all real-time control feedback processes and utilizes virtual cells to allocate radio resources to users. However, this design also results in significant potential mutual interference and deteriorates the communication reliability. To address this issue, we propose introducing multi-reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology, aiming to enhance the PMN's resilience to interference during the more challenging uplink process. Unlike conventional networks, the PMN faces not only the lack of real-time channel state information (CSI), but also the unknown transmission requirements of users. Therefore, managing RISs to serve PMN is an arduous task. We propose a scheme that trains the long short-term memory network (LSTM) using joint CSI, which is iteratively updated with an asynchronous advantage actor-critic (A3C)-based method over time scales. This enables the acquisition of predicted CSI, thus achieving accurate control of RIS to suppress interference. The simulation results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, demonstrating an improvement of over 21% in the probability of successful physical connections between users and access points (APs), compared to schemes based on outdated CSI and time-correlated CSI.

articleTitle: Deep Viewpoint Prediction in 360º Video with Data Distribution Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Tile-based 360º video transmission approaches in-volve accurate prediction of the user's viewpoint trajectory. Current models still exhibit significant prediction errors for videos with high viewpoint dispersions, increasing the likelihood of low-quality of user experience. This issue may be attributed to the considerable variations in users' viewpoint data distribution when watching such videos. To address this problem, this paper proposes a deep viewpoint prediction model in 360º Video (DVP360). The model extracts spatio-temporal features of both image and viewpoint information through convolutional neural networks (CNN). It then employs Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to contextually combine these spatio-temporal features. Finally, we adjust the model parameters through knowledge transfer, which enhances the model's ability to adapt to variable data distributions, thereby improving prediction performance. Numerical results indicate that DVP360 outperforms baseline methods on the MMSYS18, CVPR18, and PAMI18 datasets, where especially, the prediction error is reduced by 18.7% on the MMSYS18 datasets.

articleTitle: Attention-Enhanced Rainbow DQN for Cell Reselection in Satellite Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In satellite communication networks, user devices can be in either active or idle states. In active states, devices actively communicate with specific cells, maintaining a continuous connection for data transmission. In idle states, however, user devices do not actively communicate with specific cells but need to monitor potential cells and perform cell reselection (CR) under appropriate conditions for future connections. Inefficient CR decision-making is a significant issue in these states, particularly in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks characterized by large-scale and highly dynamic environments. To address the inefficiency in CR decision-making under these conditions, especially when dealing with a varying number of candidate satellites, we first model the reselection problem as a Markov decision process. By incorporating a self-attention mechanism for candidate satellite correlation modeling and adjusting the related network structure, we propose an Attention-Enhanced Rainbow DQN algorithm. This algorithm improves the model's learning ability and decision stability in tasks involving a varying number of candidate satellites. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms weighted decision algorithms and conventional Rainbow DQN algorithms in terms of load balancing, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and the number of reselections.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning on Homomorphically Encrypted Data
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The need for encrypted machine learning arises from the growing concern over data privacy and security in the era of big data and artificial intelligence. This study examines the performance of machine learning (ML) models on homomorphic encrypted data using the CKKS encryption scheme. We evaluated various models, including k-nearest neighbors (KNN), logistic regression (LR), and convolutional neural networks (CNN) on diverse datasets, including the Titanic, Pima Indians Diabetes, MNIST, and Fraud Detection datasets. Our experiments compare the performance of these models on encrypted and unencrypted data to assess the impact of encryption. The results demonstrate that while encryption introduces a slight performance degradation, the accuracy loss remains within acceptable limits. For instance, the logistic regression model's accuracy on the Titanic dataset was 82.72% for plain data, 81.36% for encrypted data with a polynomial degree of 4096, and 82.00% for a polynomial degree of 8192. The MNIST CNN model achieved 99.4% accuracy on plain data, 98.0% with 4096, and 99.0% with 8192. Our findings highlight the practical applicability of encrypted machine learning in preserving data privacy without significantly compromising performance, offering valuable insights for future research and development in secure machine learning systems.

articleTitle: Lightweight RF Fingerprint Identification using Cross Modal Knowledge Distillation: Learning from Wired to Wireless
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) is considered as a feasible zero-trust IoT identification, however, the presence of channel effects in wireless propagation significantly impacts its identification performance. In this paper, we propose a cross modal knowledge distillation based RFFI network (DrffNet) to mitigate the channel effects. Specifically, in our proposed DrffNet network, wired and wireless long range (LoRa) RF signals are jointly used as inputs to the teacher network and student network, respectively. By transferring the RFF knowledge from the hidden layers of the teacher network, the student network can achieve effective RFFI that is resilient to the channel effects. The student network used for RFFI of a similar performance has a parameter size of only 10.68 MB, achieving a 27% reduction compared with the teacher network. We conduct experiments with real-world datasets of the LoRa devices and analyze the feasibility of the proposed network via the ablation experiments. The results demonstrate that our proposed network achieves an identification accuracy of above 95% under various channel environments. Additionally, we show that the proposed network outperforms the benchmark convolutional neural network (CNN) networks on RFFI.

articleTitle: Delay-Aware Probabilistic Cache Placement for Scalable Videos in Satellite-Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid expansion of video services, caching has emerged as a promising solution to reduce retrieval delay and alleviate backhaul pressure. Specifically, caching video content on user devices and satellites is particularly effective for users without ground base station services. However, addressing the challenge of meeting users' varying video quality demands while reducing content transmission delay is critical. Therefore, this paper investigates a layered caching scheme based on Scalable Video Coding, which encodes videos into different layers to provide various quality levels and caches video content on different nodes. Furthermore, an optimization problem for the probabilistic cache placement scheme in a multi-layer caching model is proposed and solved using the Quasi-Oppositional Whale Optimization Algorithm. The simulation results indicate that, compared to other algorithms and benchmark schemes, the proposed scheme effectively reduces transmission delay.

articleTitle: Dynamic User Clustering for MIMO-NOMA Network: Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To enable the base station to serve more users, we implement multiple-input multiple-output non-orthogonal multiple access, which is capable of serving multiple users with a single beam. Therefore, it is crucial to group users according to their channel correlation before performing beamforming. Heuristic methods are commonly used, as the user clustering problem is NP-hard. However, these methods do not sufficiently utilize the information obtained through exploration. We use discrete soft actor-critic deep reinforcement learning for user clustering to achieve better performance. The performance of the heuristic method is affected by the predefined number of clusters as well, which makes it impractical. To address this issue, we modify the output of the clustering algorithm with the probability of a user belonging to a cluster and introduce several virtual clusters to generate empty clusters. This enhancement allows certain clusters to remain unselected by any user, leading to the formation of empty clusters, and enabling dynamic adjustment of the number of clusters based on real-time network conditions. Simulation results have demonstrated that our proposed dynamic clustering algorithm outperforms traditional clustering methods and leads to the optimal number of clusters.

articleTitle: Dynamic Deployment for User-Centric Multi-UAVs Communications with Fairness Consideration
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In recent years, the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as temporary aerial base stations (ABSs) to provide services to mobile users has shown tremendous potential. However, traditional UAV-centric deployment strategy fails not only to fully leverage the flexibility of UAVs, but also to guarantee the fairness among multiple mobile users. Therefore, in this paper, a user-centric multi-UAVs communications network is constructed, where the adjacent mobile users are dynamically clustered, so that the position of each UAV ABS can be adaptively changed according to the time-varying user-centric clusters. To attain the fair throughput of the conceived network, a genetic algorithm assisted multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (GA-MADRL) method is proposed, which meticulously designs the positions of multiple UAVs and multiple access resources to enhance the user fairness of each constructed user-centric cluster. Simulation results show that, compared to the conventional UAV-centric deployment scheme, the proposed scheme significantly improves the fair throughput.

Index Terms: Speed Of The Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

articleTitle: Dynamic Resource Allocation in Integrated Terrestrial-Satellite Networks: An Elastic Decision Transformer Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The integration of terrestrial and satellite networks offers broader coverage and higher capacity, meeting the rising demand for connectivity. This paper presents a novel resource allocation approach for integrated terrestrial-satellite networks by utilizing an Elastic Decision Transformer (EDT) to optimize user association and power control. EDT, based on the Decision Transformer (DT), which incorporates trajectory stitching and dynamic history length adjustment, can effectively handle dynamic and complex environments. Different from traditional reinforcement learning methods, which require retraining in new scenarios with varying input numbers, EDT leverages the transformer's ability to process variable-length inputs with ensuring adaptability and fast convergence. Simulation results that the proposed EDT-based approach shows robust convergence, superior generalization capabilities, and scalability across various network scenarios, highlighting its effectiveness in optimizing resource allocation in next-generation communication networks.

articleTitle: Joint Design of Trajectory and Near-Field Beamforming for STAR-RIS-Enabled ISAC
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) can be assembled in the air-ground integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) to further enhance the performance. However, the near-field effect should be further considered with higher carrier frequency and increasing number of STAR-RIS elements. In this paper, we propose a STAR-RIS enabled air-ground near-field ISAC scheme, where the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is deployed as a mobile base station and the semi-passive architecture is adopted to alleviate the severe path loss. We maximize the weighted sum rate to guarantee both the communication and sensing by modifying the beamforming vectors, the reflection/transmission matrices and the hovering location of UAV to match the near-field effect. To address this challenge, we first divide it into three subproblems, which are recast into convex ones by the semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation. Finally, we develop an alternate algorithm to iteratively solve them. Simulation results are shown to demonstrate the superiority and validity of the proposed scheme.

Author Keywords: simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface

articleTitle: CQI Generation for AI-Enabled CSI Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based channel state information (CSI) feedback (CSF) is a promising technique for next-generation cellular networks, drawing interest from both academia and industry. This method uses an autoencoder to compress and reconstruct the channel matrix's eigenvector into a precoder, known as implicit CSI. The existing CSF mechanism also requires user equipment (UE) to estimate the signal-to-noise ratio using implicit CSI to adapt the channel quality indicator (CQI) for different modulation and coding schemes. However, AI-based implicit CSF presents significant challenges for CQI generation. Specifically, since the UE only has access to the original perfect CSI rather than the reconstructed CSI, coupled with the sample-level instability of AI, there is a non-negligible mismatch between the precoder known at the UE and that applied at the base station, thus significantly degrading the accuracy of CQI and affecting the transmission rate. Addressing this issue, we propose a proxy-based CQI generation algorithm for AI-based implicit CSF. A lightweight neural network is generated at the UE by knowledge distillation to imitate reconstructed CSI. Thus, the CSI mismatch on both sides is minimized at a low cost, facilitating accurate CQI generation. Simulation results confirm that the proposed algorithm improves CQI accuracy and leads to a 21.64% increase in data rate, all achieved with extremely low complexity.

articleTitle: Rate Grouping Based Non-Orthogonal Random Access Aided by Online Traffic Load Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With user collision being the main concern for massive random access, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is an important tool to address the issue because it allows users to share the same channel resources. However, more refined access control schemes are expected in consideration of the explosively increasing traffic in modern communication systems. In this paper, we aim to maximize the access ratio with the aid of traffic load prediction and NOMA technique. The user equipments (UEs) are divided into groups according to their rate requirements. Given the grouping policy, the overall access success probability is analyzed based on Shannon capacity limits. A dynamic programming-based resource grouping algorithm is proposed to optimize the grouping policy of resources. The grouping optimization procedure depends on the output of a knowledge-driven online traffic load predictor, which gives the specific prediction of the traffic in each rate group. The proposed scheme is user-friendly because the prediction and the grouping optimization are both carried out at the base station (BS). Numerical results proved the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme over non-grouping schemes.

articleTitle: Merged-r Luby Transform Coded Computation for Non-Linear Tasks in Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Coded computation has garnered considerable attention for its ability to eliminate the stragglers' effect. Most existing works of coded computation are designed for linear tasks. They cannot handle the nonlinear tasks directly, leading to high computation, transmission and decoding latency. In this paper, considering a nonlinear task in wireless networks, we propose an efficient merged-r Luby transform (LT) coded computation scheme. First, we give the merged-r LT coding strategy to reduce the computation and transmission costs. Then, the maximum degree decoding (MDD) strategy is proposed to speed up the decoding process. Finally, we analyze and optimize the latency performance for the whole network by designing the merging parameter. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that our proposed scheme has significant advantages over the existing ones for nonlinear tasks.

articleTitle: DFRL-DS: A Diffusion-based Reinforcement Learning Algorithm in Discrete Actions for Base Station Energy-saving Control
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The exponential growth of mobile traffic is escalating energy usage in global mobile networks. Newer cellular technologies like 5G, while offering increased throughput and reduced latency, also require more power for denser base station layouts and more demanding processors. Improving energy efficiency is critical for the design of future mobile networks. In response to these challenges, we propose a novel algorithm combining reinforcement learning (RL) and diffusion models in discrete actions (DFRL-DS) for energy-saving control of base stations. Our proposed algorithm, DFRL-DS, stands at the forefront of this endeavor, offering a sophisticated control strategy that is both adaptive and efficient. We represent the forward process (noise addition) of the diffusion model as the training process of the policy network, and the reverse process (denoising) of the diffusion model as the decision- making process of the policy network. In addition, we devise a new mechanism for the reward function of RL. Through experiments, our algorithm achieves significant energy conservations while maintaining an acceptable level of Quality of Service (QoS). On average, DFRL-DS saves 49% to 59% energy compared to baseline algorithms and 20% to 42.5% compared to other popular deep reinforcement learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Near-Field Attitude and Location Estimation Based on Partitioned Large-Scale Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper studies a passive localization system, where a single base station (BS) is employed to estimate the position and attitude of a mobile station (MS). The BS and the MS are equipped with uniform rectangular arrays (URAs), and the MS is located in the near-field region of the BS array. To avoid the difficulty of tackling this problem directly based on the near-field signal model, we establish a subarray-wise far-field received signal model. In this model, the entire BS array is divided into multiple subarrays to ensure that the MS is in the far-field region of each BS subarray. By exploiting the angles of arrival (AoAs) of the MS antennas at different BS subarrays, we formulate the attitude and location estimation problem under the Bayesian inference framework. Based on the factor graph representation of the probabilistic problem model, a message passing algorithm named array partitioning based pose and location estimation (APPLE) is developed to solve this problem. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed APPLE algorithm outperforms other baseline methods in the estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Modulation and Coding Techniques Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Traditional Adaptive Modulation and Coding (AMC) techniques rely on real-time and accurate Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) estimates, but often resulting in suboptimal data transmission performance in scenarios with significant link transmission delays and rapid channel changes. This paper introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm to enhance traditional AMC techniques. By applying Q-learning principles to define the RL framework, including state space, action space, and reward, this study proposes a Q-learning-based AMC technique.
