Leveraging RL's robust perception and decision-making capabilities in uncertain environments, this method mitigates the shortcomings of traditional AMC techniques, such as coarse channel state partitioning and mismatched state lookup tables, especially in dynamic channel conditions, thereby reducing resource inefficiencies and enhancing system throughput. Evaluation of spectral efficiency and bit error rate under conditions of rapid channel changes and SNR estimation errors due to feedback delays reveals that the Q-learning-based AMC technique achieves superior performance compared to threshold-based AMC methods.

articleTitle: Enhanced Specific Emitter Identification Using Multi-Sampling Convolutional Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the proliferation of modern electromagnetic equipment and the rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT), ensuring physical-layer security has become a critical concern. Specific Emitter Identification (SEI) methods are es-sential for identifying devices and protecting national security within the IoT environment. Despite the effectiveness of many radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting techniques based on deep learning (DL) and raw I/Q signals, current DL methods for SEI face limitations in learning short-term and long-term features simultaneously and fail to adaptively emphasize effective features. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Multi-Sampling Convolutional Attention Network (MSCAN)-based SEI method. Our approach leverages a multi-sampling signal pro-cessing module to extract multi-scale features and incorporates a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention block to enhance the discriminative ability of these features, thereby improving the model's performance without increasing computational costs. The effectiveness of the proposed MSCAN method is validated on an open-source dataset, achieving an accuracy of 95.3%.

articleTitle: Self-Sustainable IRS Assisted Covert Communications: Analysis and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has been widely applied to establish an environment suitable for covert communications, which hides the existence of transmission behavior. Unfortunately, the existing IRS usually relies on battery/grid power supply for its operations, which limits its performance and is even unprocurable in covert communications. To address the above dilemma, a self-sustainable IRS with active reflection elements is considered in this paper to facilitate covert communications, where the IRS is powered by wireless energy harvesting (EH) from the incident signals. To reveal the benefits brought by the self-sustainable IRS for covert communications, the covert rate and the detection error probability at the warder are derived to evaluate the transmission effectiveness and covertness. Besides, the covert rate maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing beamforming vectors, jamming power, EH-related factor and reflection coefficient matrix. Further, to solve this non-convex problem, an alternating optimization-based algorithm is proposed by exploiting semidefinite programming and successive convex approximation techniques. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme compared with the existing benchmarks, where energy self-sustainability and multiplicative-fading mitigation are achieved by the self-sustainable IRS. In addition, a non-trivial tradeoff exists between covert rates and self-sustainability, providing insights into the optimal number of reflection elements and the deployment position of the IRS.

articleTitle: Joint Waveform and Passive Beamforming Design for IRS-Aided ISAC via Deep Unfolding
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has become a promising technique to alleviate the spectrum congestion via sharing the same spectrum for communication and sensing. Nevertheless, many ISAC schemes encounter the challenges of high complexity. In this paper, we propose a dual-functional waveform design scheme for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided ISAC based on deep unfolding learning. Specifically, the weighted sum of multi-user interference energy and waveform discrepancy is minimized via the joint waveform and phase-shift design. We first develop an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) based iterative algorithm to handle the non-convex optimization problem. Then, we develop a deep unfolding neural network (NN), named ADMM-NET, which unfolds the proposed ADMM-based iterative algorithm to a layer-wise architecture. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed ADMM-NET.

articleTitle: STAR-RIS-Enabled Anti-Jamming Design for Secure Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this work, an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework with presence of jammer, which enabled by a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (STAR-RIS) is proposed. The jammer exists in the reflective region and interferes communications, which is considered as an extended target. Then, the Cramér-Rae bound (CRB) for estimating the jammer's response matrix is derived. To maximize the achievable rate (AR) of the transmission user, we jointly optimize the active and passive beamforming, while satis-fying the reflection users' AR constraints, the transmission power budget, the CRB for target estimation constraint and the STAR-RIS coefficient matrices constraints. Based on the alternating optimization and successive convex approximation algorithms, the original problem is decomposed into two subproblems, and each subproblem is solved by using fractional programming (FP) and semidefinite relaxation (SDR) theorem. The simulation results verify the feasibility of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust Image Watermarking Based on Texture Guidance and Dynamic Multi-Spectrum Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Tracking image sources and verifying copyright information is crucial in digital media communication. Digital image watermarking technology, widely used for copyright protection and source tracking, faces challenges in balancing imperceptibility and robustness under a certain embedded capacity. To address this problem, this paper proposes a robust image watermarking framework based on a deep invertible network, named DRIN. Based on the frequency-domain characteristics of robust steganography, we parallelly introduce a texture guidance module (GLCM) and a dynamic fine-grained DCT representation-based channel attention module (DFscaNet) into the network. These modules guide the model to effectively locate the texture features where high-frequency energy is concentrated in the cover image, improving the quality of the watermarked image and enhancing the robustness of the watermark. Experiments have demonstrated that the proposed method has superior performance, higher visual quality, and stronger robustness compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Auto-encoders in PHY: Principles and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deep learning has significantly impacted the physical layer of wireless communications, leading to rapid advancements in this field. Auto-encoder, a self-supervised learning framework, has demonstrated substantial success across various domains. With the continuous improvement of computing power, research on introducing auto-encoders into physical layer wireless communication systems continues to deepen. In this paper, we explain the principles of auto-encoders and explore their applications in communications, particularly in waveform design, joint source-channel coding, and channel representation learning. We further review recent progress, identify key challenges beyond computational limitations, and propose potential future research directions.

articleTitle: Decformer: A Multi-model Fusion Method Based on Decomposition and Transformer for Industrial Energy Consumption Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As the industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) advances, the need for precise and effective long-term energy consumption forecasting grows more critical. Addressing this challenge relies on the technology of Time Sequence Forecast (TSF). Some ad-vanced deep learning methods have been used for TSF. However, existing work suffers from overly complex model structures and a lack of consideration for characteristics of the specific data. Therefore, we propose a time series prediction method called Decformer based on sequence decomposition and multi-model fusion. For components exhibiting strong periodicity, we use a simplified Transformer model with channel-independence processing to efficiently extract time-dimension feature information. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art time series prediction methods.

articleTitle: A Q- Learning and Fuzzy Logic Based Routing Protocol for UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the development of ad hoc network technol-ogy, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm has demonstrated significant promise across civil and military domains. However, owing to unique attributions, such as high dynamic topology, 3-D mobility and low density, it's extremely challenging to establish a reliable and robust communication between flying nodes. In this paper, we proposed a Q-Learning and Fuzzy Logic based Routing Protocol (QFRP) for UAV networks, which adopted an efficient Q-value update mechanism based on HELLO and ACK. In this mechanism, we take neighbor set coherence and link lifetime into account. Since routing exploration has an important impact on routing performance, we proposed a fuzzy logic based mechanism for exploration and exploitation that considers Q-value, link quality and access delay to mitigate the blindness of random exploration. Simulation results demonstrate that QFRP can make efficient routing decisions within dynamic multi-hop UAV networks, and outperforms existing protocols regarding packet delivery ratio (PDR), end-to-end (E2E) delay, and routing overhead.

articleTitle: Joint Resource Allocation and Data Offloading for Closed-Loop Controls in Satellite-UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To efficiently provide coverage for the machines and robots in remote areas, satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be utilized. In such scenarios, UAVs need to integrate different functions to support the control tasks of robots efficiently, while satellites can serve as backhaul to the cloud. To improve the overall performance of the closed-loop control tasks of robots, we jointly optimize the communication and computing resource allocation with data offloading. Specif-ically, we explore the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost to measure the control performance and formulate a sum LQR cost minimization problem. An iterative algorithm is proposed to solve the optimization problem. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Beam Structured Channel Estimation for Massive MIMO with Beam Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the channel estimation for massive multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. By utilizing the beam based statistical channel model (BSCM), the aim is to estimate the beam domain channel and then convert it to the space-frequency (SF) domain channel. The problem is solved by the EM algorithm based on beam completion with information geometry theory. By completing the measurement matrix to a unitary matrix, we can get the equivalent received signal model, and then the model manifold and data manifold related to the a posteriori distribution of channel are built separately. The optimal distribution is obtained by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>-projecting and m-projecting alternately between these two manifolds. We demonstrate that the EM algorithm based on beam completion can converge to MMSE estimator with low complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve better performance than existing methods when the number of iterations is small.

articleTitle: Semantic Communication Based on Content Style Adaptation for Image Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The development of semantic communication has promoted the research on image transmission. Content and style are two crucial characteristics of image information. Existing studies have explored image information transmission and recovery methods in semantic communication systems, but do not consider both image style information and content information simultaneously. To address this issue, based on deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) structure, a novel system named semantic communication based on content style adaption (CSASC) for image transmission is proposed in this paper. Specifically, a novel semantic information extraction method are designed to extract the semantic content information and semantic style information of images, meanwhile an image content-style adaptive reconstruction method is proposed by fusing semantic content and semantic style features to improve the image reconstruction accuracy. In addition, the impact of the weighting of semantic style and content information on image reconstruction quality is analyzed. Results demonstrate that the proposed method has better recovery results compared with existing image semantic communication methods.

articleTitle: Channel-Estimation-Free Gradient Aggregation for OFDM Over-the-Air Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: We investigate gradient aggregation in over-the-air federated learning (OA-FL) with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), where the parameter server (PS) employs a combining vector to estimate the aggregated gradient. By lever-aging the block-wise linear property between the subcarriers, we propose a novel channel-estimation-free (CE-Free) gradient aggregation scheme for OFDM OA-FL. In this scheme, the combining vector at the PS is linearly approximated, avoiding the requirement to train combining vectors for subcarriersindivid-ually, and thereby significantly reducing the required number of training symbols. We analyze the aggregation performance of the proposed scheme by characterizing the aggregation mean square error (MSE). Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation Based on Clustered Interference Alignment with Redundant User Extraction in Ultra-Dense Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a resource allocation scheme with clustered interference alignment (IA) in Ultra-Dense Networks (UDNs). Our goal is to maximize the sum spectral efficiency (SE) of users according to the network distribution and provide additional subchannels for redundant users as well as ensure fairness of the primary users, while other works mainly consider the Degrees of Freedom (DoFs) demand of users, ignore how well one DoF can achieve and treat IA cluster as the object of subchannel allocation. Our method takes the coherence bandwidth as the minimum resource where precoding and equalizing of IA become effective in all resource blocks. We construct a weighted graph at first to cluster users with their corresponding small base stations into disjoint and different sizes of groups. Second phase, we utilize graph coloring to allocate primary subchannels to groups of users to achieve fairness. Then we propose a redundant user extraction scheme to allow users free of interference to join in primary subchannels of other cluster to increase sum SE of the network. Simulation results indicate in a certain transmit signal to noise ratio (transmit SNR) interval, the proposed solution has obvious advantages over existing scheme, promising for further research.

articleTitle: Spatial Bandwidth of Bilateral Near-Field Channels for Linear Large-Scale Antenna Array System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper analyzes the spatial bandwidth of line-of-sight (LoS) channels in massive MIMO systems. For the linear large-scale antenna arrays (LSAA) of transceivers placed in random locations in 3D space, a simple but accurate closed-form expression is derived to characterize the spatial bandwidth. Subsequent analysis of the LSAA's spatial bandwidth properties is also provided, leading to the formulation of an approximate expression for the effective degrees of freedom (EDoF) of bilateral near-field channels. Interestingly, as proved in this work, when the transmit and receive arrays are coplanar, with the receive array positioned perpendicular to the axis joining the centroids of the transmit and receive arrays, the EDoF of the LoS channel is found to be approximately maximized.

articleTitle: Short - Term Temperature Forecasting Using LSTM -CatBoost Combination Method
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a fast-growing technology that has the potential to revolutionize various aspects of our daily life, such as weather forecasting. Accurate weather forecasting allows people to prepare for sudden weather changes, reducing property damage caused by weather disasters. Traditional long short-term memory (LSTM) is good at modeling long-term dependencies, but it has the problem of overfitting. In view of this, categorical boosting (CatBoost), a machine learning model having strong forecasting ability and not easy to overfit, is employed to enhance weather forecasting accuracy. By combining these two powerful and heterogeneous models, an LSTM-CatBoost averaging method, which has both low variance error and bias error in principle, is proposed to forecast weather-related variables, e.g., temperature. This study uses the data from the IoT-based automatic weather station deployed across Botswana to conduct experiments, and the results show that the proposed LSTM-CatBoost averaging method outperforms other benchmark models, including the individual LSTM and CatBoost prediction model. This indicates that the proposed method is more suitable for short-term weather forecasting in relevant regions of Botswana than some existing mainstream methods.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Data Hybrid-Driven Low-Energy Resource Allocation in Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Due to the growing demand for services and the dense deployment of base stations, the substantial energy consumption has emerged as a significant impediment to the development of cellular networks. Although numerous energy-efficient methods have been proposed, the energy consumption of cellular networks continues to exhibit an upward trend. This is because the existing methods may provide superfluous services to users to achieve higher energy efficiency, resulting in extra energy consumption. In this paper, a low-energy resource allocation method is proposed to minimize the total energy consumption, considering the long-term service demand of each user. However, this problem is challenging to solve due to the the interaction of resource allocation across sequential time slots, such as data queuing and service satisfaction. Therefore, the initial problem is decoupled into multiple subproblems to relax complexity by Lya-punov optimization. Moreover, a knowledge-data hybrid-driven deep reinforcement learning framework is proposed to solve each subproblem. Specifically, the knowledge module is embedded into DRL to make decisions for low-energy based on exact service demand, without requiring extensive exploration and learning. Simulation results show that the energy consumption of the proposed method is reduced by 20.7% compared with the baseline, and the convergence speed is increased by two times.

articleTitle: Joint Beamforming and User Association Design in Active RIS-Aided Cell-Free URLLC System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is considered as a promising technology thanks to its strong ability to reflect incident signals and modify propagation properties of wireless environment. In this paper, we investigate the sum-rate maximization problem for active RIS-aided cell-free multipleinput multiple-output (CF-MIMO) system in ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC) scenario. Specifically, a two-timescale user-RIS match optimization scheme is proposed to reduce the required channel training and feedback overhead, where beamforming matrices at the remote antenna unit (RAU) and active RIS are jointly optimized under the maximum transmit power constraints. Since the problem formulated is non-convex, an alternating optimization algorithm is proposed, wherein the original optimization problem is decomposed into transmission and association subproblems that can be efficiently solved. For the former subproblem, auxiliary variables are introduced in accordance with the successive convex approximation (SCA) method to overcome the non-convexity, while for the latter subproblem, a penalty-based association scheme is proposed to tackle the non-convex discrete user-RIS match constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms the baseline schemes in terms of spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Secure Beamforming Design Based on Multistatic Cooperative Sensing via IRS
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we study the multistatic cooperative sensing assisted secure transmission via intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). To be specific, a multistatic cooperative sensing scheme is proposed to obtain the angle of arrival and the localization of the eavesdropping target to achieve the beam alignment accurately. Our goal is to maximize the sum secrecy rate by jointly optimizing the association variables of base station (BS) and users, the BS beamforming and the IRS phase shifts, subject to the requirement of target sensing. Due to the coupling of variables and nonconvex objective function, we decompose it into three subproblems and develop an alternative algorithm to solve them iteratively. The association variables are first obtained by successive convex approximation. Then, the BS transmit beamforming can be derived via the semidefinite relaxation. Finally, an alternating direction method of multiplier is adopted for the IRS phase-shift design. Simulation results indicate that the multistatic cooperative sensing via IRS can enhance the sensing performance and guarantee the security.

articleTitle: DRL Based on Priority Evaluation for Collaborative Perception Task Offloading in Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the explosive growth of the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs), autonomous driving has received numerous attention from academia and industry. However, the limited perceivable range of a single connected and automated vehicle (CAV) leads to missing real-time road condition information, which affects driving safety. Meanwhile, due to the complexity of applications and dependencies between tasks, perception tasks require high computing capability and low latency. However, a CAV has limited local computing capability, it is necessary to offload perception tasks to edge for processing. Therefore, to improve perception coverage and reduce perception task processing la-tency, we propose a Priority Evaluation and Deep Reinforcement Learning Task Offloading (PDRTO) algorithm. Firstly, a dual layer IoVs architecture for task offloading is constructed to improve the perception coverage of CAVs and achieve safe driving through collaborative perception among CAVs. At the same time, considering task dependency and CAV's mobility, a multi-CAV collaborative perception task graph is proposed to model the optimization problem of minimizing the processing delay of perception subtasks. Then, the optimization problem is transformed into a multi-objective mixed integer optimization problem, and solved by the proposed PDRTO algorithm to minimize the processing delay of perception tasks. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other compared algorithms in improving CAV perception cover-age and reducing perception task latency.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Access Point Sleep Control in User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of energy efficient access point (AP) sleep control in user-centric cell-free massive MIMO (CFmMIMO) systems is investigated. The large-scale deployment of AP in CFmMIMO makes it challenging to obtain an effective AP sleep policy in real time. For this consideration, we propose to use a proximal policy optimization (PPO) based deep reinforcement learning method, which has advantages in solving high-dimensional problems, to obtain an energy-efficient AP sleep strategy. We map the continuous action generated by PPO agent into discrete domain and design a specific reward for PPO to train which guarantees the quality of service (QoS) requirement of users. Simulation results show that our proposed method outperforms the state-of-art benchmark methods.

articleTitle: Semi-Passive Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces Aided Channel Estimation for Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) have appeared as a cutting edge strategy to augment channel estimation and amplify network efficiency in high-mobility vehicular networks. The semi-passive IRS contains semi-passive and passive elements, and changing the phase of these elements can enhance control of signals precisely. In this paper, the semi-passive IRS aided channel estimation is investigated to mitigate the multipath fading and channel error, thereby improving the achievable rate and channel estimation accuracy. This novel methodology is presented by the implementation of phase optimization of the IRSdynamic channel estimation technique and IRS deployment strategy. In IRS aided channel estimation, the Spatial Base Extended Model (SBEM) algorithm is used to simplify the uplink channel estimation process and the Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) the IRS phase to improve the channel estimation accuracy. Simulation result shows the method can to significantly improve the communication efficiency and channel estimation accuracy within the high-mobility vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Near-Lossless Compression of Two Independent Binary Sources with One Encoder
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the near-lossless compression of two distinct but independent binary random sources <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, both of which are asymmetrical independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) sources. In particular, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> is assumed to be sparser than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex>. We show that, to efficiently compress <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, explicit source coding (compression) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> (the sparser one) is not required. The basic idea is to encode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> with an error-correction code and then superimpose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> on the codeword. Hence, only one encoder-decoder pair (EDP) suffices to compress two sources. Theoretical analysis shows that the proposed coding scheme is entropy-approaching in terms of bit-error rate (BER) of both sources, and numerical results verify our analysis. Furthermore, we analyze the complexity of compression using the block Markov superposition transmission-repetition (BMST-R) codes to discuss the advantage of the proposed scheme. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme compresses the two sources simultaneously in a more compact way but causes no performance degradation.

articleTitle: Transmission Design for STAR-RIS Assisted Dual-User Uplink MIMO Based on Statistical CSI
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) is employed to assist uplink dual-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications, which can create virtual links from users in both transmission and reflection region to the base station throughout the entire space, thereby enhancing coverage and reducing energy consumption. We aim to jointly design the transmit covariance matrix for the two users and the phase shift matrices for the STAR-RIS, based solely on statistical channel state information. The implemented alternating optimization algorithm for joint design is achieved by utilizing the derived closed-form expression of the ergodic sum rate. Specifically, the optimal transmit covariance matrices for the two users are determined using a water-filling algorithm, meanwhile the suboptimal solutions for the phase shift matrices of the STAR-RIS are obtained via the projection gradient ascent method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior system performance.

articleTitle: ECN - Based Packet Loss Differentiation for Adaptive TCP in LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks are becoming increasingly important for next-generation communication technologies due to their wide coverage and low latency. However, the changing network topology and high packet loss rates in LEO networks pose challenges for the traditional Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), which has difficulty distinguishing between congestion-induced packet loss and other types of loss. This problem leads to a significant reduction in throughput and bandwidth utilization. In this paper, we propose a new TCP protocol named LOTCP (Loss-Optimized TCP), which employs Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) to distinguish between congestion loss and non-congestion loss. LOTCP utilizes handover information and satellite bandwidth data to make these distinctions. It relies on ground stations and Software-Defined Network (SDN) controllers to monitor network conditions, allowing TCP to adjust the congestion window more effectively in response to congestion events. Simulation results indicate that LOTCP delivers significantly improved throughput compared to existing protocols. This research presents a promising approach for optimizing TCP performance in LEO satellite networks.

articleTitle: A Novel Modulation Classification Scheme Based on Meta-Transfer Learning with Limited Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A novel meta-transfer learning based modulation classification (MTMC) scheme is proposed in this paper, addressing the limitations of deep learning based modulation classification schemes that almost cannot leverage unlabeled data. MTMC effectively leverages unlabeled data and rapidly adapts to new modulation patterns with limited labeled samples. By integrating the strengths of meta-learning and transfer learning, our approach mitigates overfitting issues associated with traditional meta-learning methods for complex networks with small datasets. The MTMC framework comprises three stages: pre-training a network using transfer learning, meta-training by migrating network parameters, and fine-tuning for rapid classification of new tasks. Simulation results demonstrate that the MTMC scheme can significantly enhance feature generalization ability and improve modulation classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Traffic Prediction Based on Graph Convolutional Network for LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The accurate prediction of traffic load is of critical importance for the design of efficient routing and load balancing schemes for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, which greatly affect the utilisation of inter-satellite links. However, the periodically changing topology of satellite networks leads to significant uncertainty in the traffic dynamics, making it difficult to predict. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the characteristics of satellite network traffic and proposes a traffic prediction algorithm based on Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (TemGCN). The proposed scheme addresses a gap in the field of satellite network traffic prediction by leveraging the network topological structure and making full use of the highly dynamic but periodically changing topology characteristics of satellite networks. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme is more accurate and robust than other existing schemes.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Deraining Network Based on Hash Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Rain streaks frequently result in severe visual degradation and occlusion of the foreground, significantly hampering the execution of visual tasks in outdoor scenes. Currently, the majority of image deraining methods heavily rely on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Nevertheless, the crucial issue of balancing computational cost and deraining performance remains unresolved. Therefore, we propose a deraining network based on hash attention to achieve a balance between rain removal performance and computational complexity. To reduce computational complexity, we design the Hash Transformation Attention Block (HTAB), which enables fast filtering and extraction of input feature information. Additionally, to enhance the quality of feature learning, we propose the Controlled Feature Transformation Block (CFTB), which introduces a feature control mechanism to adjust the detailed complementarity between information flows at multiple levels. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network HAD-Net achieved outstanding image deraining performance with relatively low computational cost.

articleTitle: Secrecy Rate- Distortion Tradeoff for Integrated Sensing and Communication With an Untrusted Sensing Node
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) tech-nology combines communication and sensing functionalities through a unified signal waveform. While this integration offers potential benefits such as improved spectrum sharing and reduced processing costs, it also poses security challenges. Specifically, when the communication receiver and sensing entity operate as separate nodes, maintaining message secrecy from the sensing entity becomes crucial. To address this challenge, we propose a two-receiver state-dependent ISAC model that includes an untrusted sensing node. In this model, the ISAC transmitter aims to convey a message to the communication receiver while enabling the sensing of channel state for an untrusted sensing receiver, all while keeping the message secret from the untrusted sensing receiver. We consider the fundamental tradeoff between secure communication rate and sensing distortion within this model, which is characterized by the secrecy capacity-distortion function. To establish an inner bound on the secrecy capacity-distortion tradeoff region, we adopt an input-constrained wiretap coding approach. In addition, we present an outer bound on the tradeoff region by independently deriving the necessary conditions on the rate and on the sensing distortion. We also provide two illustrative examples that highlight the utilities of these bounds and demonstrate the superiority of the unified signal waveform over a separation-based approach via time-sharing.

articleTitle: Task-Oriented Service Provision and Scheduling for Non-Terrestrial Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The non-terrestrial network (NTN) receives considerable attentions due to the development of the sixth generation technologies in recent years. However, the mobility and heterogeneity of satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles in NTN lead to increasing challenges in resource allocation and management. As such, the network function virtualization technology is introduced, by deploying service function chains (SFCs) to achieve requirements. However, it brings conflicts and resource competition due to urgent unexpected tasks. Therefore, scheduling multiple SFCs in NTN is a crucial issue. In this paper, a task-oriented service provision and scheduling model is proposed to tackle the dynamic complexity of NTN by designing the reconfigurable time extension graph. Subsequently, the SFC scheduling problem is formulated to maximize the number of completed tasks within limited resources and time constraints. Due to the problem form of integer linear programming, we propose a deep reinforcement learning based algorithm. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, indicating its superior performance over other benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Joint Task Offloading and Service Caching for Vehicular Edge Computing with Energy Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) enables vehicles to offload their tasks to idle vehicles for processing. To process tasks, the needed service model should be stored ahead. Considering the storage of vehicles is limited and downloading the service model upon tasks causes repeated data transmission, it is necessary to determine which service models should be cached and which tasks should be offloaded. For vehicles, the task completion time is crucial due to their mobility nature. Therefore, balancing the completion time and energy consumption for vehicles with limited battery capacity in highly dynamic system remains a significant challenge. To address this, we jointly designed task offloading and service caching scheme to minimize the tasks completion time in a cache-assisted VEC scenario while satisfying the long-term average energy constraints. We adopt Lyapunov optimization and Deep reinforcement learning (D RL) based Task offloading and Service caching (LDTS) to solve the proposed problem. Specifically, the Lyapunov optimization is used to tackle the issues of long-term energy consumption constraints by transforming the original problem into per-slot optimization problems that can be resolved using a model-free DRL method. Simulation results demonstrate that the LDTS method can minimize the completion time while satisfying the constraints of the long-term energy consumption budget. The results indicate that the LDTS method outperforms other benchmark methods.

articleTitle: A Novel Patch Selection Approach for Quality Assessment on Short-Form Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Video quality assessment (VQA) on short-form videos plays a critical role in optimizing online multimedia systems. Traditional VQA approaches have made significant progress with the widespread applications of deep learning. However, the quality assessment of short-form videos has re-ceived insufficient research attention with limited performance, neglecting the unique perceptual characteristics of human over short-form videos, e.g., large transfer distance and scattered distribution of fixations. In this paper, we propose the patch selection VQA (PS-VQA) approach to promote this field by incorporating human attention mechanisms during short-form video viewing. In our PS-VQA approach, we first introduce a patch selection network (PS-Net) to identify the patches most relevant to perceived video quality in short-form videos. Subsequently, we develop a quality assessment network (QA-Net) to extract both local and global quality-aware features from the selected patches to predict the overall video quality. Extensive experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed VQA approach on short-form videos. Interestingly, our ablation experiments show that accurately assessing the quality of a short-form video merely requires 5 % pixels of the whole frame.

articleTitle: A Bayesian Optimization Approach for Online System Configuration of Edge Video Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Surveillance cameras have been extensively deployed in urban areas. The captured video data requires real-time analysis, e.g., target detection and classification, to complete specific tasks, such as traffic control and public safety monitoring. Thanks to the advance of edge computing technology, hardware-constrained cameras can offload computationally intensive video analysis tasks to edge servers, alleviating the prolonged latency issues associated with traditional cloud-based video analytics. Constrained by the wireless transmission capacity, it is necessary to dynamically configure the resolution of video frames and the communication bandwidth to balance the video analysis accuracy and transmission delay. In practice, a major design difficulty is the lack of explicit models that describe the delay and accuracy of edge inference as a function of the configuration choices. For this, we propose an online algorithm based on Bayesian Optimization (BO) to jointly optimize the resolution selection and bandwidth allocation of edge video analytics systems on-the-fly. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed BO-based method has comparable average performance as the “black-box” deep reinforcement learning algorithm, while achieving greater temporal stability and much higher fairness among the users. The results have showcased the importance of model interpretability offered by the BO-based method in enhancing the performance of dynamic edge video analytics systems.

articleTitle: Robust Joint Optimization for Multi-Cell Backscatter Communication System: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Backscatter communication(BackCom) has emerged as an ultra-low power technology that enables battery-free devices for various Internet of Things scenarios. To improve the network performance, the resource allocation is important; however, most of prior works developed the strategy under the ideal case, i.e., the channel state information (CSI) is perfect, which can worsen the performance. Hence, in this paper, we investigate the robust resource allocation for a multi-cell BackCom system, where the imperfect CSI is considered. To maximize the sum rate of the considered system, a robust deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm is developed by jointly optimizing spectrum allocation, the reflection coefficients of tags, and the transmit power of readers. Specifically, the original non-convex optimization problem is transformed into a Markov decision process. Then, to effectively handle the discrete-continuous hybrid action space, we propose a robust multi-agent parametrized deep Q-network (MAPDQN) algorithm, where the artificial distorted CSI is introduced during the training phase to compensate for the error of imperfect CSI. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Beamforming with Projection-Based Covariance Matrix Reconstruction Under Colored Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Extant adaptive beamforming techniques employ the interference-plus-noise covariance matrix (INCM) to safe-guard the desired signal from suppression. In the presence of colored noise, null offsets may occur, resulting in degradation of beamformer performance. To bolster the beamformer's ro-bustness under colored noise, a novel reconstruction method for the INCM is proposed. This method initially estimates the steering vector of the desired signal by integrating the principal eigenvalue and projection methods. Subsequently, the colored noise covariance matrix is reconstructed utilizing the properties of the blocking matrix. Ultimately, the power of the interference signal is obtained through the projection of the received data, thereby yielding the INCM. The computational complexity of the proposed algorithm stands favorably in comparison to that of other algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that this method exhibits strong robustness to mismatch errors under colored noise, regardless of whether the SNR is high or low, or whether the number of snapshots is high or low.

articleTitle: Sensing-Communication-Security Enhanced Integrated Satellite and Terrestrial Network with Active Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Integrated satellite and terrestrial network (ISTN), while beneficial, faces security vulnerabilities due to wireless communication's open nature, leading to potential eavesdropping and interference. This paper addresses these challenges by leveraging the characteristics of low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites and active reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS). LEO satellites' periodic coverage gaps reduce the need for continuous interference with eavesdroppers. Active RIS, capable of amplifying and optimizing reflected signals, mitigates multiplicative fading without increasing transmission power. The proposed scheme enhances the security and energy efficiency of ISTNs. An alternating optimization algorithm, based on Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) and Successive Convex Approximation (SCA), balances the active RIS's power constraints and the need for secure and efficient communication. Furthermore, the integration of Dual-Function Radar Communications (DFRC) base stations with Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) capabilities improves the precision of eavesdropper detection and interference. Simulation results corroborate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in significantly reducing the target SINR at the eavesdropper, thereby improving the secrecy gain.

articleTitle: Dual Propagation Video Super-Resolution with Spatial-Temporal Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The key success of existing Video Super-Resolution (VSR) methods lies primarily in exploring temporal and spatial information, typically relying on feature alignment and reconstruction. However, existing alignment methods are generally based on optical flow warping, where linear interpolation may not be accurate in some cases. Additionally, existing reconstruction modules usually employ stacked residual blocks, which are constrained by the locality inductive bias of CNNs and struggle to model global spatial features effectively. To address these issues, we propose a novel Dual Propagation Spatial-Temporal Attention Network (DPSTAN) for VSR. Specifically, we propose a Coarse-to-Fine Cross-Attention (CFCA) feature alignment module, incorporating a learnable resampling structure to achieve better alignment. Moreover, we propose a Residual Efficient Extended Channel Attention Block (RE2CAB), which extends the traditional channel attention mechanism to effectively explore the spatial information. Experiments on public datasets have demonstrated that our proposed method improves both quantitative evaluation and visual effects compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Camouflaged Object Detection with State-Space Model
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) remains a challenging task in computer vision due to the intrinsic similarity between camouflaged objects and their backgrounds. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexities of camouflage. In this study, we propose a novel COD framework, SSM-COD, which employs a state-space model (SSM) to effectively distinguish camouflaged objects. Our approach leverages the dynamic properties of SSM to capture both global and local correlations, enabling robust detection in complex environments. We conducted comprehensive experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets: CODIOK, CAMO, and CHAMELEON. Rigorous testing and ablation studies demonstrate that SSMCOD significantly outperforms existing COD techniques in detection accuracy and reduces missed detections. These findings highlight the transformative potential of the state-space model in enhancing COD performance and indicate promising directions for future research aimed at improving the robustness and applicability of camouflaged object detection systems.

articleTitle: A Non-Cooperative Transmitter Localization Algorithm Based on Deep Learning with Time-Frequency and Spatial Angular Information
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The precise localization of non-cooperative transmitters is crucial for security applications and daily life. However, traditional geometry-based positioning techniques suffer from large errors due to multipath effects and nonline-of-sight (NLOS) propagation. We propose a novel non-cooperative transmitter localization algorithm that leverages deep learning to overcome these limitations. Inspired by fingerprint-based positioning, our approach utilizes readily obtainable information at the receiving end, including spectrum sensing, power spectrum analysis, and spatial angle information obtained through beamforming. By integrating this information, the algorithm effectively utilizes NLOS paths, often discarded in conventional methods, to achieve more accurate source localization. Our proposed system demonstrates a positioning accuracy of approximately 2.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>.

articleTitle: PLMS: A Packet Loss Memory-based Transmission Enhancement Scheme for GEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Geostationary earth orbit (GEO) satellites are vital components of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6G$</tex> communication networks. However, GEO satellite networks face two main challenges. On the one hand, the long round-trip time makes the retransmission mechanism in the traditional transmission protocol slow to respond, which restricts the transmission performance. On the other hand, congestion packet loss caused by multi-stream competition and link packet loss due to high bit error rate coexist in GEO satellite networks, which makes it difficult for traditional congestion control (CC) algorithms to distinguish and make appropriate control decisions. To tackle these challenges, we propose a packet loss memory-based transmission enhancement scheme (PLMS). PLMS first modifies the TCP retransmission mechanism to accelerate the retransmission speed and enable the retransmission of packets that are lost again. Furthermore, PLMS introduces the packet loss memory mechanism to discern transmission link conditions, distinguish packet loss types, and dynamically adjust the sender's behavior. The mechanism can prevent misjudging bit error packet loss as congestion packet loss, thus improving CC accuracy. Our experimental results demonstrate that PLMS significantly boosts the throughput of existing CC algorithms. Specifically, under conditions of the 1 % packet loss rate caused by bit errors, the throughput of CUBIC, BBR, and Hybla increase by 945%, 9.5%, and 154%, respectively.

articleTitle: Hybrid CRB Analysis for Location Sensing in UAV mmWave Systems Under Jittering Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems are vulnerable to the inevitable UAV jitter, the impacts of which on both communications and sensing become more detrimental in the high frequency millimeter wave (mmWave) band. While the UAV jittering effects on communications have been intensively investigated, those on sensing have so far drawn little attention. In this paper, we investigate the location sensing performance of the UAV mmWave system in the presence of jitter. To this end, we identify that the location sensing performance under jittering effects is determined not only the deterministic target's location, but also random instantaneous attitude angles of the UAV. Based on this identification, we derive the closed-form expression of the hybrid Cramer-Rao bound (HCRB) and its approximation to characterize the location sensing performance of our considered system, revealing how the UAV jitter introduces extra location sensing error. Through numerical results, we validate our HCRB analysis. Moreover, we show that the detrimental effects of UAV jitter can be well alleviated by increasing the number of measurements.

articleTitle: Joint Transmit and Reflective Beamforming for Multi-Active-IRS-Assisted Cooperative Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper studies multi-active-intelligent-reflecting-surface (IRS) cooperative sensing, in which multiple active IRSs are deployed in a distributed manner to help the base station (BS) provide multi-view sensing. We focus on the scenario where the sensing target is located in the non-line-of-sight (NLoS) area of the BS. Based on the received echo signal, the BS aims to estimate the target's direction-of-arrival (DoA) with respect to each IRS. In addition, we leverage active IRSs to overcome the severe path loss induced by multi-hop reflections. Under this setup, we minimize the maximum Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) among all IRSs by jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming at the BS and the reflective beamforming at the multiple IRSs, subject to the constraints on the maximum transmit power at the BS, as well as the maximum transmit power and the maximum power amplification gain at individual IRSs. To tackle the resulting highly non-convex max-CRB minimization problem, we propose an efficient algorithm based on alternating optimization, successive convex approximation, and semi-definite relaxation, to obtain a high-quality solution. Finally, numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness of our proposed design and the benefits of active IRS-assisted sensing compared to the counterpart with passive IRSs.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Modeling of Cellular-Connected UAV Networks with NOMA scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The integration of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), a new type of Aerial User (AU), into terrestrial cellular networks to form a cellular-connected UAV network has emerged as a significant research topic in the field of communications. However, the introduction of AUs competes for channel resources with Terrestrial Users (TUs), which can lead to a deterioration in the performance of TUs. Taking into account the channel differences between AUs and TUs, this paper utilizes a Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) scheme to enhance the spectral efficiency of the network. Utilizing tools from stochastic geometry and queueing theory, we propose a spatiotemporal analytical model to analyze the network performance from both spatial and temporal perspectives. Based on this framework, we first calculate the average queue length and average waiting time to quantify the system's temporal performance. Following this, we derive the successful transmission probability for both AUs and TUs, and subsequently obtain the average ergodic rate for the entire network. This comprehensive approach enables a thorough understanding of the network's performance across both spatial and temporal domains.

articleTitle: Interference Management for IRS-NOMA Networks via Constructive Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Owing to the ability of reconfiguring wireless channels, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) can help non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) to release its tremendous potential. However, the inter-user interference becomes the bottleneck of IRS-NOMA networks. To tackle this challenge, we propose two constructive interference precoding (CIP) based countermeasures for interference exploitation in IRS-NOMA networks. Specifically, the first scheme makes the interference from higher-order users (HUs) be constructive to lower-order users (LUs), so that the interference-free decoding can be achieved. While the second scheme utilizes the interference from LUs for the signal reception of HUs to avoid successive interference cancellation (SIC). The transmit power is mini-mized by jointly optimizing the BS active and the IRS passive beamformings for the two schemes. To solve each scheme, we apply successive convex approximation (SCA) and alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. Simulation results are presented to show the superiority and applicability of the proposed schemes compared to benchmarks.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Method for Open-set Wireless Signal Detection in HF Band
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Wireless signal detection (WSD), which aims to detect and identify signals of interest in the wideband spectrum, is an important part of non-cooperative high frequency (HF) receivers. However, in HF band, WSD remains a challenging task due to the complexity and openness of HF environments, and the presence of unknown signal types may severely affect detection performance. To improve detection performance and robustness, this paper focuses on the deep learning-based methods and proposes a multi-signal detection neural network (MDNN) for open-set WSD in HF band. The proposed network utilizes multi-resolution spectrograms (MRS) of the received wideband signal to estimate the frequency range and signal type of each narrowband signal in the wideband spectrum. In addition, prototype learning and metric learning are also applied to learn discriminative feature representations of different signal types for distinguishing between known and unknown signal types. The experimental re-sults indicate that the proposed method outperforms the baseline methods in both closed-set and open-set HF environments.

articleTitle: An Air Quality Oriented Convolutional and Interaction Network for Traffic Flow Prediction in VANET
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To accurately predict traffic flow, it is necessary to take into account not only the volume of road traffic, but also external urban factors. Particularly, the correlations between urban air quality and traffic flow is particularly strong, However, due to the complexity of air composition and its nonlinear characteristics in spatial and temporal sequences, it remains underexplored in current research efforts. In this paper, we propose an air quality oriented convolutional and interaction network for traffic flow prediction in Vehicular ad-hoc network, AQCInet, which captures feature information from both types of data using convolutional block, integrates this feature information with interaction networks, and effectively represents the long-term and short-term dependencies in the sequential data, ulti-mately outputting short-term traffic flow prediction results. The experimental results show that AQCInet can effectively model traffic flow sequences with complex time dynamics by aggregating rich features from multiple resolutions. Compared with existing model, our proposed model significantly improves RMSE, MSE, and MAE through jointly considerations of the relationship between air quality, various air component concentrations, and traffic flow.

articleTitle: Joint Scatterer and AoA Map Construction Based on Limited Channel Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the context of 6G mobile communication networks, achieving centimeter-level positioning accuracy necessitates a comprehensive understanding of wireless signal propagation environments. However, CKM construction usually requires a large amount of channel measurements to achieve the desired accuracy. Besides, the wireless channel information is usually more dynamic as compared with the scatterer distribution on physical map. To this end, this paper proposes the joint construction of scatterer and AoA map based on the limited channel measurements. For scatterer map construction, we first group the AoA measurements into various LoS and NLoS clusters and then estimate the scatterer edges based on the virtual transmitter corresponding to each cluster. For AoA map construction, we first establish the spatial correlation model and obtain the complete AoA map via the classical spatial interpolation method. Then, the obtained AoA map is further refined based on the constructed scatterer map. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithms can considerably improve the map accuracy as compared with the traditional spatial interpolation methods.

articleTitle: Design of Task Distribution and Scheduling Strategies for Data Processingin the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To adapt to the characteristics of IoT tasks arriving online (i.e., the arrival pattern and time of tasks cannot be pre-dicted), delay sensitivity, and limited processing unit resources, to ensure the completion of tasks with low latency and to ensure the efficient and stable operation of the IoT platform, this paper studies the problem of online task distribution and scheduling in the unit manager of a data-driven Internet of Things (IoT) architecture. The problem is modeled and an efficient online task distribution and scheduling algorithm is proposed, named OnSche. We have validated the performance of the OnSche algorithm using real datasets and conducted a thorough verification. The experimental results show that under different parameter changes, OnSche is consistently superior to the baseline methods.

articleTitle: On the Performance Bounds of Steganographic Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Steganographic coding is a fundamental technique in adaptive steganography, and the introduction of polar codes has significantly enhanced its security. However, the performance of steganographic polar codes has primarily been evaluated through experiments, and their construction has remained some-what heuristic. This paper theoretically presents an optimal model for steganographic polar codes based on a analysis of their performance bounds, by examining the relationship between polar code decoding and steganographic coding based on polar codes. Although this model can only be constructed approximately, numerical simulations indicate that the proposed optimal construction offers improved security performance compared to classic codes.

articleTitle: Fluid Antenna-enabled Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The current integrated sensing, communication, and computing (ISCC) systems face significant challenges in both efficiency and resource utilization. To tackle these issues, we propose a novel fluid antenna (FA)-enabled ISCC system, specifically designed for vehicular networks. We develop de-tailed models for the communication and sensing processes to support this architecture. An integrated latency optimization problem is formulated to jointly optimize computing resources, receive combining matrices, and antenna positions. To tackle this complex problem, we decompose it into three sub-problems and analyze each separately. A mixed optimization algorithm is then designed to address the overall problem comprehensively. Numerical results demonstrate the rapid convergence of the proposed algorithm. Compared with baseline schemes, the FA-enabled vehicle ISCC system significantly improves resource utilization and reduces latency for communication, sensing, and computation.

articleTitle: MRIB: Robust Task-Oriented Communication for Multi-Device Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In recent years, task-oriented communication has gained significant attention for its ability to extract and transmit necessary information for downstream tasks. However, multi-device collaboration scenarios pose challenges for task-oriented communication, such as encoding and fusing multimodal data and ensuring robustness in complex communication environ-ments. To address these challenges, we propose the Multi-device Robust Information Bottleneck (MRIB) scheme, which considers channel conditions in multi-device scenarios and introduces a new information bottleneck optimization objective. This objective is used to optimize the framework through end-to-end training and we derive a variational upper bound to facilitate the effective optimization of the framework. We validate the MRIB framework in both unimodal and multimodal scenarios, demonstrating its superiority over existing task-oriented communication methods, especially in environments with diverse and noisy data inputs. Experimental results show that MRIB offers better robustness and reasoning performance compared to baseline methods. Future work will focus on further optimizing the framework and exploring its applications in more complex communication environments.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Scheme for Efficient RIS-Assisted Massive MIMO Sparse Channel Representation and Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To realize the full potential of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, the acquisition of accurate channel information is crucial. However, the high-dimensional cascaded channel considering its underlying structured sparsity makes efficient channel estimation scheme design a challenging task. This paper develops a novel two-stage scheme for efficient RIS-assisted massive MIMO channel estimation where the methods for sparse channel representation and recovery are respectively designed. For the former, we develop a random search orthogonal matching pursuit (RSOMP) algorithm to exactly estimate the common angles of arrival at the base station side, based on which the dimension of sparse representation dictionary for the high-dimensional cascaded channel can be significantly reduced. The remarkable thing is that it can efficiently cope with the off-grid error caused by direction mismatch between the fixed sampling grids and the random directions of angles. For the latter, to relieve the high-computational complexity involving matrix inversion when calculating the posterior of channels, we develop a pattern-coupled covariance free expectation maximization (PC-CoFEM) algorithm, which simultaneously exploits the underlying block-structured sparsity of channels. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed schemes can achieve superior performance to comparison schemes as well as illustrate the effectiveness for sparse channel representation and recovery.

articleTitle: An Efficient Graph-Based Approach for Periodic Earth Observation Over the Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Periodic observation is widely used for information collection in emergency scenarios such as earthquakes, wildfires, and floods. Multi-satellite observation is needed to achieve pe-riodic observation due to the limited observation capability and long revisit period of a single satellite. Choosing when and which satellite to observe the target to achieve periodical observation can be challenging. Existing efforts adopt a time-consuming method to solve the problem. They also ignore some feasible solutions. Moreover, the classical mathematical programming method can also take a long time to solve the problem. Therefore, we propose a graph-based periodic scheduling method. First, we formulate the problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem, which is non-convex and intractable. To address this, we introduce a periodic observation graph model that transforms the original problem into a path-finding problem. We then propose a graph-based periodic observation path construction algorithm. Numerical simulations under the settings of a realworld satellite network demonstrate that the performance of our scheme is significantly faster than the baselines and can obtain observation offsets.

articleTitle: Channel Characteristics-Based Domain Adaptation for Multiuser MISO Beamforming Design
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deep learning-based beamforming solutions face the issue of channel mismatch when the communication environment changes. Although existing adaptive solutions, such as meta-learning, can solve the channel mismatch, there are still have two disadvantages. They rely on labelled data in the fine-tuning stage, and the characteristics of channel state information (CSI) has not been fully explored and transferred, which are important for improving adaptation performance. To address these challenges, the paper first proposes a novel domain adaptation framework based on channel correlation characteristics for sum rate maximization (SRM), named DA-SRM, which does not require labelled data during the transfer process. Then, two transformer units with different attention mechanism are applied to explore the long-range dependence characteristics of CSI. Simulation results show that the proposed DA-SRM and transformer-based DA-SRM achieve better adaptation performance than existing beamforming adaptive solutions.

articleTitle: AoI-aware DAV Data Collection Based on the IRS's Phase Estimation in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), ensuring the real-time and reliable collection of state information is crucial for maintaining the efficient operation of the network. To ensure freshness of information in delay-sensitive applications such as autonomous driving, this paper combines Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) technologies to deal with the IRS-aided UAV online data collection problem. In the formulated problem, the average Age of Information (AoI) of sensor nodes (SNs) is minimized by jointly optimizing the IRS's phase shifts, the UAV's trajectory, and SN association. The problem is divided into two coupled subproblems: the IRS's phase control and UAV's data collection. We propose the framework of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to deal with the two subproblems individually, referred to as PPO-Dual. In particular, given the UAV's position and SN association, the optimal phase shifts of the IRS is estimated using PPO based on the partial channel state information (CSI) obtained by sending pilot signals through some active elements mounted on the IRS. Based on the well trained IRS's phase estimation strategy, the UAV's online data collection scheme is also determined using PPO. Simulation results show that the proposed PPO-Dual algorithm can effectively estimate the IRS's phase shifts and achieve the average AoI performance close to that under perfect CSI conditions.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Image Transmission Over Semantic Communication Enabled UAV Swarm Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, a semantic communication framework is proposed for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm formation flight. In the studied model, a leader extracts semantic information from the aerial image and transmits it to each follower using limited transmission power. The borders of obstacles are referred to semantic information of the aerial image. Based on the received semantic information, each follower reconstructs semantic maps for trajectory planning so as to maintain formation and avoid obstacles. We use the metric of Intersection over Union (IoU) to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed semantic communication network. The problem is formulated as an optimization problem whose goal is to maximize the sum of IoUs of all followers. To solve this problem, a semantic information selection and power allocation (SISPA) algorithm based on reinforcement learning (RL) framework is proposed. The proposed SISPA algorithm enables the leader to evaluate the importance of semantic information, and, thus efficiently allocating transmission power and selecting important semantic information to improve the sum of IoUs. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with the traditional wireless communication networks without semantic communication techniques, the proposed approach yields a 17.4% improvement in terms of the sum of IoUs.

articleTitle: Joint Power and Trajectory Control for Integrated Satellite-USV-Terrestrial Maritime Rescue System
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To address the frequent occurrence of sudden sea accidents, this paper investigates a USV-enabled maritime rescue system (MRS). We integrate satellite and terrestrial base stations with the maritime wireless network (MWN) to achieve seamless communication and control coverage. Considering the spatiotemporal variability of ocean currents, we establish USV kinetics and MRS-oriented transmission models. We formulate a rescue time minimization problem, where communication power and USV trajectory control are jointly optimized. By decomposing the problem, we derive and solve two sub-problems iteratively. In particular, we propose an innovative hydrodynamic deep-Q learning network algorithm to plan current-favorable trajectories. Simulation results underscore the efficacy of the integrated MWN and the hydrodynamic-informed approach in enhancing sea rescue missions.

articleTitle: Digital Image Semantic Communications with Joint Source-Channel Coding and Constellation Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Recently developed semantic communication facilitates an intelligent and minimalist approach to meet the growing demands for future sixth-generation (6G) communication sys-tems. However, since the constraints of backpropagation during neural network training, the predominant approach of most extant studies are based on differentiable channel inputs, which is difficult to match with existing digital communication systems effectively. Meanwhile, the research on modulation techniques considering constellation optimization for digital semantic communication is still in the early stage. To deal with these issues, we propose a novel deep joint source-channel coding (DJSCC)-based digital semantic communication with considering constellation optimization, which is referred to as DJSCC-C. Firstly, the digital semantic communication system is introduced. Secondly, the DJSCC-C system is proposed for image transmission, which is trained with a newly-constructed loss function, aiming to improve the transmission rate in the digital semantic communication system as well as optimize the joint source-channel coding capability. Finally, simulation results are provided to verify the superiority of the proposed scheme for future design of digital semantic communication systems.

articleTitle: Modeling and Performance Optimization of Slotted Aloha with Successive Transmission
