However, as the DL-based AMC becomes increasingly widespread, it is faced with the severe secure issue from various adversarial attacks. Existing defense methods often suffer from the high computational cost, intractable parameter tuning, and insufficient robustness. This paper proposes an eXplainable artificial intelligence (XAI) defense approach, which uncovers the negative information caused by the adversarial attack through measuring the importance of input features based on the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). By properly removing the negative information in adversarial samples and then fine-tuning(FT) the model, the impact of the attacks on the classification result can be mitigated. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SHAP-FT improves the classification performance of the model by 15%~20% under different attack levels, which not only enhances model robustness against various attack levels but also reduces the resource consumption, validating its effectiveness in safeguarding communication networks.

articleTitle: Saliency Prediction of Traffic Surveillance Videos: A Benchmark and A Multi-Task Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Traffic surveillance videos are crucial for the devel-opment of intelligent transportation systems. The huge number of these videos has introduced significant challenges for storage and transmission, etc. Therefore, efficient and accurate video saliency prediction (VSP) can benefit a wide range of video processing techniques for traffic scenes, such as video compression, smart navigation, and traffic event detection. However, currently there are no VSP approaches or eye-tracking datasets dedicated to traffic surveillance videos. In this paper, we establish a large-scale eye-tracking dataset, dubbed traffic surveillance videos 1K (TSV1K). TSV1K contains 1000 high-quality traffic surveil-lance videos, with eye-tracking annotations from 30 subjects. Based on our dataset, we conduct thorough analysis on the correlations between human attention and traffic scenes, e.g., vehicle distribution and scene complexity. Accordingly, we pro-pose a multi-task traffic saliency prediction network (MTTS-Net), which leverages the task of traffic salient object detection (TSOD) to promote the performance of the VSP task. In order to better learn these tasks, a two-stage training strategy is developed to progressively train the MTTS- Net. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in both tasks of TSOD and VSP on traffic surveillance videos. Our dataset and code are available on https://github.com/giteec/TSV1K.

articleTitle: Edge-Featured Graph Attention Network for Power Control in Cell-Free and D2D Heterogeneous Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cell-free and device-to-device (D2D) heterogeneous networks can effectively enhance spectral efficiency. However, spectrum reuse among different transmission links leads to severe interference to limit the growth of network capacity. In this paper, we propose a power control algorithm based on graph attention network for interference coordination in cell-free and D2D heterogeneous networks. Specifically, a heterogeneous graph is utilized to model the power control problem, where desirable transmissions and interference are represented as edges of different types. The edge-featured attention mechanism is applied over the constructed graph to capture the relationships among various edges. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm can improve network capacity and exhibit generalization performance with respect to network scales.

articleTitle: Optimizing Age of Information for Multi-Antenna Aided Covert Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The performance of wireless communication systems has been improved with the recent advances in array antenna technology. In this paper, we propose a scheme to improve the age of information (AoI) for covert communication with multi-antenna technique (MAT). Specifically, we first propose the transmitter structures and the corresponding beamforming methods for the considered model. Subsequently, the closed-form expressions of the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence is derived to serve as the quantitative measure of communication covertness under both schemes, based on which the average covert AoI (CAoI) is derived to jointly characterize the covertness and timeliness performance. Then, to minimize the average CAoI, the optimization problems of the blocklength and beamforming parameters are formulated and solved. Finally, the numerical results are provided to show that the proposed scheme indeed improve the covert communication performance in terms of the average CAoI.

articleTitle: Near Field and Far Field Mixed Communication Via Rate Splitting Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss communication between near and far field mixed channel in traditional massive MIMO networks. In this network, space beams are pre-configured to cater to near-field users. We introduce a groundbreaking model, which is a communication model in which users within a distance smaller than Fraunhofer distance use space division Multiple Access (SDMA) and the rest use Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) in the case of near and far field mixed channels. A successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm was proposed to solve a maximizing the minimum rate of user communication problem. The results of this study show that the user rate of RSMA-based near and far field hybrid communication is much higher than that of a single RSMA or a single SDMA, highlighting the synergistic potential of combining SDMA and RSMA to seamlessly adapt to near and far field communication scenarios. In addition, the study shows that augmenting the quantity of base station antennas is able to significantly enhance the massive MIMO systems' rate performance, thus enhancing the proposed method's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Authentication Based on CNN-GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (loT) has created significant opportunities for the future of telecommunications. Research on physical layer authentication with channel features holds promise to improve wireless network security for loT devices. In this paper, we exploit Channel State Information (CSI) phase extracted from the receiver with multiple antennas to enhance the channel spatial diversity. Then Convolutional Neural Network and Generative Adversarial Network (CNN-GAN) model is designed for physical layer authentication. Outlier score from model is introduced to authenticate device identity. Finally, we carry out extensive experimental evaluations about the authentication performance and robustness of the proposed scheme by data collected from Wi-Fi signal based on IEEE 802.11n protocol. The results have successfully demonstrated that the proposed scheme exhibits outstanding performance.

articleTitle: A Lightweight and Anonymous MAKE for LDACS
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The L-band Digital Aeronautical Communication System (LDACS) plays an important role in ensuring the security of future aeronautical communications infrastructure. However, the establishment of LDACS security design is still complicated because lots of authentication messages need to be transmitted while air-to-ground channel resources are limited. And it lacks anonymous measures to avoid tracking by malicious entities and enhance the security of the authentication process. In contrast to the traditional protocol, we propose a lightweight LDACS Mutual Authentication and Key Establishment (MAKE) protocol with anonymous identity and conduct a security and performance comparison analysis of the protocols in this paper. The analysis results show that the proposed protocol can well achieve the security goals of LDACS, and can well protect the privacy of stations. The number of air-to-ground communication interactions from cell-attachment to mutual authentication has also been reduced to five times, and the total communication cost is 4578 bits.

articleTitle: An Online Approach to Balancing the Energy Consumption for IoT Sensors in UAV-based MEC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider an unmanned aerial vehicle-enabled (UAV-enabled) Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) Internet of Things (IoT) system consisting of multiple energy harvesting devices. In the system, the UAV acts as the edge computing platform providing computation service to the devices. We assume that the energy and sensing data arrive at the devices stochastically. As the amount of energy harvested by devices can differ significantly, we attempt to balance the energy consumption among devices thus avoiding the loss of devices due to the depletion of the battery energy. To ensure energy fairness, we employ an a-utility function, which incorporates the device's remaining energy and energy expenditure. Without any future knowledge of the data and energy arrivals, our objective is to design an online algorithm to jointly optimize the long-term system throughput and utility, while satisfying the stability requirement of the data queue. We formulate the problem as multi-stage stochastic programming that involves functions of time averages and propose an online algorithm based on the perturbed Lyapunov optimization technique. Due to the time-coupling of different variables, we first transform the original problem into a multi-stage stochastic optimization problem involving only time averages. Then, we utilize the Lyapunov optimization method to decouple the transformed problem into a series of per-slot deterministic subproblems. In each slot, we alternatively optimize the auxiliary variables, the data sensing rate, the computation offloading, the communication resource allocation, and the trajectory of the UAV. Simulation results show that the online algorithm can maintain the stability of the data queue. Additionally, we observe a tradeoff between the system's lifetime and throughput when adjusting the parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>, as well as a tradeoff between throughput and delay for the Lyapunov method.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Beam Prediction: A Deep Learning-Based Approach With Compressed Multi-Beam Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Aided with artificial intelligence, a great deal of beam management methods aiming to reduce the training overhead have emerged. However, these codebook-based approaches are confined to decrease the number of measured beam pairs and ignore the compressibility of the measured beam data. In this paper, we propose a novel beam prediction framework that leverages compressed multi-beam measurement as the model input and jointly optimize the multi-beam compression and reconstruction process via deep learning. Specifically, we build a spatial-temporal beam prediction based on compressed sensing, and design a neural network to infer the optimal beam pair for transceivers with reduced training overhead. Simulation results show that the proposed beam prediction approach outperforms the existing AI-based solutions even at a high moving speed with almost negligible increase in model storage overhead as well as computational complexity.

articleTitle: Linear Precoding for Faster-Than-Nyquist Signaling with Imperfect Channel State Information
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) transmission over frequency-selective fading channels, it is essential to eliminate both FTN-induced intersymbol-interference (ISI) (FTN-ISI) and channel-induced ISI (channel-ISI). Although frequency domain equalization (FDE) techniques can mitigate channel-ISI at the receiver, their performance is often inadequate. In contrast, cyclic prefix/suffix (CPS)-G-to-minus-half (GTMH) precoding shows superior effectiveness in mitigating channel-ISI. However, existing CPS-GTMH precoding techniques assume the transmitter obtains perfect channel state information (CSI) estimated at the receiver. This is impractical due to the high latency in satellite communication links. Therefore, this paper explores precoding for FTN signaling under imperfect CSI (ICSI) and proposes CPS-minimum mean squared error (MMSE) and linear pre-equalization (LPE)-MMSE precoding schemes based on the MMSE criterion. Both schemes employ a cyclic prefix to transform the channel-ISI matrix into the circular matrix, thereby avoiding inter-block interference. The primary distinction is that CPS-MMSE precoding handles FTN-ISI and channel-ISI together using MMSE precoding. In contrast, LPE-MMSE precoding addresses FTN-ISI with LPE and channel-ISI with MMSE precoding separately. Simulation results indicate that CPS-MMSE and LPE-MMSE precodings outperform CPS-FDE and LPE-FDE in mitigating channel-ISI when the estimation error is 0.005 and 0.01. For instance, with a packing ratio of 0.9, a roll-off factor of 0.25, and an estimation error of 0.01, CPS-MMSE and LPE-MMSE precodings achieve bit error rate (BER) gains of approximately 0.8 dB and 1 dB at a BER of 1e4, respectively. However, when the estimation error increases to 0.1, the BER performance of CPS-FDE and LPE-FDE surpasses that of the CPS-MMSE and LPE-MMSE precodings, indicating the proposed precoding schemes' unsuitability for larger channel estimation errors.

articleTitle: Multiuser Interference Suppression: A Generalized Nearest Neighbor Decoding Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The architecture of the proposed generalized nearest neighbor decoding (GNND) is investigated under quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) and utilized for multiuser interference suppression. The GNND is capable of handling the non-Gaussian inter-stream interference effectively, for multiuser channels under QPSK input, while the conventional channel linearization (CL) approach generally fails. Adopting the information-theoretic tool of generalized mutual information (GMI) for measuring the achievable information rate, the optimal GNND in maximizing GMI is derived. A coded modulation scheme based upon GNND is further designed, via connected with the existing low-density parity-check decoders, without requiring iterations between demodulation and decoding. Numerical results show that the GNND significantly outperforms the CL approach in terms of the achievable code rate and the bit-error-rate.

articleTitle: Design Methodologies of Physical Layer Artificial Intelligence Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been introduced into the design of physical layer technologies and showed great potential in improving system performance. However, there are many open issues and challenges to be addressed. In this paper, the design methodologies of physical layer AI are investigated. The evaluation methodology and evaluation key performance indicators (KPIs) are first presented, which include the performance-related and cost-related KPIs. Furthermore, examples are given to illustrate how to integrate AI and expert knowledge, including dataset acquisition, AI model selection, data preprocessing based on expert knowledge, and auto-encoder design based on partial channel reciprocity and other available information. Some designs to enhance the generalization capability of AI models are also proposed, including low overhead auto-encoder design, transfer learning, and distributed machine learning. Finally, the standardization roadmap of physical layer AI is investigated.

articleTitle: Measurement-Based Channel Characterization and Modeling for 5G-Railways at 2.16 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Current Global System for Mobile Communications for Railway (GSM-R) is increasingly unable to meet the burgeoning demand for diversified private network communication services, such as multimedia dispatching communication and intelligent operation. Relying on mature 5G technology, 5G for Railways (5G-R) is considered to be a promising solution for realizing intelligent railways. The investigation of channel characteristics is fundamental for the design of 5G-R. However, existing research lacks comprehensive studies on channel characteristics specific to typical scenarios and unique frequency bands of 5G-R. In this paper, we carry out sufficient measurements on a dedicated 5G-R loop railway test line. Based on measurement data, we perform a comprehensive extraction and analysis of typical channel parameters, including path loss, shadow fading, small-scale fading, power delay profile, delay spread, Rice K-factor, angle of arrival estimation, and angle spread. The results will significantly contribute to design, deployment and network optimization of 5G-R.

articleTitle: Joint Beamforming Design for Semi-IRS-Aided Secure ISAC with Assistance of Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the sensing-assisted secure transmission for an integrated sensing and commu-nication (ISAC) system, where the semi-intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is deployed to facilitate the secure communication and sensing. First, we adopt the multiple signal classification algorithm to estimate the target's direction with Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) serving as the performance metric. After obtaining the information about the target, which may be a potential eavesdropper, the expression of secrecy rate related to the eavesdropper's estimation accuracy can be formulated. Then, we formulate a weighted optimization problem to maximize the secrecy rate and minimize the CRB by jointly designing the active beamforming, artificial noise and phase shifts of IRS. In particular, by considering the estimation errors, we introduce a series of beampattern constraints about the main beam in order to cover all possible angles of target, ensuring that the security is guaranteed in all directions. Accordingly, the sensing function can improve the secrecy performance through the increasing estimation accuracy in each iteration. Simulation results reveal effectiveness of the proposed scheme and the utility of sensing as a facilitator for physical layer security.

articleTitle: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Wi-Fi Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Carrier sensing multiple access with collision avoidance (CSMA/CA) is a basic medium access control (MAC) protocol specified in the IEEE 802.11 standard. However, the current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>SMA/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>A mechanism has limitations in providing high throughput and low latency services in user-dense scenarios. To address this issue, this paper investigates the distributed channel access problem based on communicative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), where each user acts as an agent, deciding whether to transmit data in the current time slot based on its local observation and the messages from other agents. We propose a novel MAC protocol, which employs a centralized training with decentralized execution paradigm. Moreover, we adopt the parameter sharing approach with positional encoding as an identifier to distinguish different agents, which further improves the network adaptability. The simulation results illustrate that the proposed Selective Communication-based Multiple Access (SCMA) algorithm: 1) outperforms the conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>SMA/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>A in terms of throughput and latency, while maintaining user fairness; 2) improves the model adaptability to accommodate varying numbers of users.

Author Keywords: decentralized partially observable Markov decision process

articleTitle: Integrated Optical Sensing, Communication, and Computation System for Quadruped Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper develops an integrated optical sensing, communication, and computation system for quadruped robot with virtual-real interaction based on digital twin technology. The system is designed to address key challenges in robotics technology, including real-time performance, low-latency control, high-precision multi-sensor data fusion, stable network transmission, user-friendly interaction interface, system scalability, and maintainability. The system comprises a number of functional modules, including a three-dimensional (3D) modeling module, a positioning perception module, a virtual interaction module, a wise sensing-transmission module, and a cloud server. The 3D modeling module is responsible for constructing the virtual quadruped robot and motion space scenarios. The positioning perception module integrates LiDAR and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data, utilizing Point-light detection and ranging inertial odometry (LIO) and HDL-localization algorithms for high-precision environmental perception and positioning. The virtual interaction module provides a user-friendly control inter-face through computer software and the HoloLens headset. The wise sensing-transmission module employs WiFi and 5G links to ensure low-latency and high-bandwidth data transmission. The optical signal, sensed via camera and LiDAR, is computed at the quadruped robot and subsequently transmitted to the cloud server via the wise sensing-transmission module, which facilitates integrated optical sensing, communication, and computation. The system is designed to run on Ubuntu 20.04 platform, offering excellent scalability and maintainability.

articleTitle: Client Selection for Federated Learning Against Poisoning Attacks on Non-IID Data
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) trains a global model using local models uploaded by clients rather than raw data, leading to the protection on client privacy. However, FL is vulnerable to malicious attacks, such as poisoning attacks, which can degrade the performance of the global model. Especially in non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) scenarios, traditional malicious client detection methods are largely ineffective. To address these challenges, we propose an algorithm termed Federated Learning with Client Selection Based on Contribution and Credibility (FL-CSBC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Specifically, we design a client contribution model based on marginal contribution and a client credibility model utilizing the Rank-Sum Ratio (RSR) in the FL training process. By adopting the concept of evolutionary clustering, we utilize the current round's contribution and the previous round's credibility to quantify the credibility of each client by computing a client score, based on which we select clients that will participate in aggregation phase. At the same time, we incorporate the root dataset on the server side and utilize the server model trained by the root dataset as the initial aggregation model for each round. We evaluate the performance of our algorithm on two public datasets with different proportions of malicious clients under non-IID scenario. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the superiority of FL-CSBC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> over a variety of baseline algorithms in terms of test accuracy.

articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming Design for Wideband Near-Field ISAC with Delay Alignment Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper studies a multi-user integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system with delay alignment modulation (DAM) in the near-field. We aim to optimize multi-path hybrid beamforming so as to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the target echo while ensuring communication users' signal-to-interference plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirements and transmit power budget. To this end, we propose an alternating optimization algorithm using successive convex approximation (SCA) technology, penalty convex-concave procedure (PCCP) and second-order cone programming (SOCP). Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and show the impact of channel model mismatch and the distance dimension introduced by the near-field model on the near-field DAM-ISAC system.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Service Caching in Large-Scale UAV-Enabled Wireless Networks with Coupled Uplink and Downlink
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the service caching performance in a large-scale unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled wireless network, in which multiple UAVs equipped with caching and computation capabilities are deployed to support multiple types of tasks generated by the terrestrial user equipment (UEs). We consider a practical-yet-challenging assumption where the uplink transmission for task offloading and the downlink transmission for results feedback are coupled, and derive analytical expressions of the successful transmission probability and successful service probability, demonstrating how they are determined by the UAV's density and operating height, as well as the service caching strategy. Through numerical results, we verify the correctness of our analysis and show that the SSP of our system can be significantly enhanced by optimizing the density and operating height of the UAVs.

articleTitle: SIMRP: Self-Interference Mitigation Using RIS and Phase Shifter Network
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Strong self-interference due to the co-located transmitter is the bottleneck for implementing an in-band full-duplex (IBFD) system. If not adequately mitigated, the strong interference can saturate the receiver's analog-digital converters (ADCs) and hence void the digital processing. This paper considers utilizing a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), together with a receiving (Rx) phase shifter network (PSN), to mitigate the strong self-interference through jointly optimizing their phases. This method, named self-interference mitigation using RIS and PSN (SIMRP), can suppress self-interference to avoid ADC saturation effectively and therefore improve the sum rate performance of communication systems, as verified by the simulation studies.

articleTitle: Channel Scenario Identification Under Varying SNR Conditions Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Identifying channel scenarios is crucial for developing and optimizing wireless communication systems in the forthcoming 6G networks. In these networks, transceivers can adjust transmission schemes and optimize resource allocation based on the identified channel scenario. This study proposes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) model to identify different channel scenarios using channel frequency response (CFR) autocorrelation. The model is trained to recognize the unique features of various channel scenarios and demonstrates strong performance under varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Additionally, transfer learning is employed to improve the model's ability to generalize to a broader range of SNR conditions beyond those used in training. With minimal data, the final two layers of the CNN model can be adjusted to adapt to new SNR conditions without requiring retraining from the beginning. The proposed deep CNN, combined with transfer learning, can effectively generalize its strong performance from known SNR conditions to new ones.

articleTitle: User Activity Detection, Channel Estimation and Sensing Parameter Estimation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 16th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As one of the key enabling technologies in 6G, cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CFmMIMO) helps to achieve a macro-diversity via a large number of distributed access points, having its potential to improve communication and sensing performance significantly. In this paper, we investigate user activity detection, channel estimation, and sensing parameter estimation in CFmMIMO systems. First, we formulate a user activity detection and channel estimation problem as a multiple measurement vectors compressive sensing problem by leveraging the sparse nature of sporadic user traffic in CFmMIMO. A two-stage algorithm is proposed to solve user activity detection, channel estimation, and sensing parameter estimation problem: the first stage detects user activity and estimates effective channel coefficients; the second stage estimates the range and angle parameters associated with active users based on the estimated effective channel coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage algorithm can provide accurate activity detection and sensing parameters estimation results.
